artigo.texto: BYD Fires Up 16 GWh Battery Plant as Ten-Millionth Dynasty Car Rolls Off the Line Published on 09/30/2026 at 16:21 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD pressed ahead on two fronts this week, opening full-scale production at a new battery facility in Shaanxi province while simultaneously notching a production milestone for its long-running Dynasty line — a dual push that underscores how deeply the automaker is vertically integrating even as its share price struggles. The Xixian plant, backed by a seven billion yuan investment, carries an annual capacity of 16 gigawatt-hours. That translates into enough cells and packs for roughly 700,000 new-energy vehicles, with an expected annual output value of eight billion yuan. For now the factory feeds BYD's own assembly lines, turning out cells, battery packs and fast-charging technology. Engineers there are already putting the second-generation Blade battery through its paces, a pack the company says can jump from 10% to 70% charge in five minutes at normal temperatures. The battery division also used Wednesday to lock in fresh partnerships with the cities of Yingkou and Liaoyang, covering carbon-free port projects and components for electric heavy trucks. Dynasty Line Reaches Eight Figures On the vehicle side, the ten-millionth car from BYD's Dynasty family left the assembly line on Tuesday, arriving less than 13 years after the Qin — the first model in the series — made its debut in 2013. The commemorative vehicle was the Da Han, which gets its official market launch on October 13. Deliveries of the new Formula S range began last Monday, and BYD is targeting monthly sales of 10,000 to 15,000 units of the series in China. To keep pace with charging demand, the company intends to have 20,000 fast-charging stations up and running domestically by year-end, alongside 6,000 abroad. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Premium Push Meets a Boardroom Reshuffle Fresh metal is arriving at showrooms at a moment when BYD needs it. Nationwide pre-orders for the new Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 opened Tuesday, with car transporters rolling out since Monday to stock the company's direct-sales outlets across China. The six-seat plug-in hybrid is aimed squarely at affluent families and business travelers — buyers whose spending supports higher average selling prices. That premium tilt matters because the volume end of the market remains brutal. Management changes took effect Tuesday: Cai Hong-ping and Zhang Min stepped down as independent non-executive directors, while Cai Hong-ping and Li Yong-zhao were appointed non-executive directors. Li Gang and Xu Tu joined as independent non-executive directors for three-year terms. Overseas Growth as a Second Pillar BYD's answer to domestic margin pressure extends well beyond passenger cars. At the IAA Transportation show in Hanover in mid-September, the company unveiled a full slate of zero-emission commercial vehicles for Europe, spanning 3.5 to 44 tonnes with new heavy trucks and models for swap-body and roll-off applications. The flagship ETT 44 electric tractor unit supports charging at up to 1.5 megawatts, enough to go from 20% to 80% in roughly 20 minutes. On the manufacturing side, BYD plans to bring the Sealion 6 to Pakistan as its first locally assembled vehicle there — a shift from pure exports toward an industrial footprint on the ground. Production is slated to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026. Spending Power Behind the Technology Analyst Dale Hall of the International Council on Clean Transportation calculates that BYD, SAIC and Geely each plowed between $1,700 and $2,750 per passenger car sold into EV research, development and production during 2025. That technological depth remains the key differentiator Chinese manufacturers hold over international rivals. The stock traded at EUR 8.53 on Wednesday, up 0.7% on the day, though it has shed 20% since the start of the year amid weak domestic demand and a punishing price war at home. Pre-market indications earlier in the week had put the shares at EUR 8.45, down 21% year-to-date. The 52-week low of EUR 8.03 now marks the line in the sand: holding above it keeps the possibility of a bottoming pattern alive, while a sustained break below could deepen the broader downtrend and trigger follow-on selling. BYD, which overtook Tesla as the world's largest electric-vehicle maker in 2025, managed to lift overseas sales by more than 130% in August. Whether that export momentum and the Ti 9's reception can offset the erosion at home is the question the coming weeks of order data will answer. artigo.texto: HANGZHOU, China, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HoyUltra 2000M is Hoymiles' newly launched full-scenario commercial and industrial (C&I) energy storage solution, developed around a simple idea: do more in the factory so less efforts will be spent on project site. With integrated system components, flexible electrical configurations and liquid cooling, the MWh-level BESS is built to simplify deployment and operate across different project scenarios. - Simplified deployment through high integration HoyUltra 2000M combines the battery, PCS, thermal management, static transfer switch (STS) and fire protection into a single system. Unlike a conventional solution that uses 10 storage containers in parallel, HoyUltra 2000M reduces the system footprint by approximately 15% with less external equipment and on-site wirings. Based on Hoymiles' estimates, the required on-site work can decrease from 46 hours to 10 hours, promising considerable construction cost savings. - Flexible configuration for different applications HoyUltra 2000M offers a capacity of up to 2.61 MWh. Its AC voltage classes cover 400V, 690V and 800V, enabling adaptation to different electrical conditions. The system also supports integration with PV and diesel generators, providing greater flexibility for C&I and multi-energy applications such as PV + wind. - Built-in STS for seamless switching HoyUltra 2000M has a built-in static transfer switch (STS) to support backup switching in less than 20 ms, maintaining continuous power supply for critical loads. - Reliable operation across challenging environments The system uses liquid cooling for both the PCS and battery, with an operating temperature range from -30°C to 55°C. It maintains rated power output at up to 50°C. HoyUltra 2000M is also equipped with cabinet-level fire protection, including smoke and temperature detection, fire suppression, interlocked ventilation and compartment explosion relief. "As C&I energy storage projects become more diverse, clients need solutions that go beyond storage capacity," said Dr. Rex Zhu, General Manager of Hoymiles' Residential and C&I Storage Business Unit in introducing the design philosophy of HoyUltra 2000M. "Electrical conditions, installation requirements, multi-energy integration, backup power and operating environments all need to be considered." With a focus on integration, flexibility, reliability and safety, HoyUltra 2000M will help more C&I customers improve energy efficiency and maximize the value of energy storage across diverse operating scenarios. Learn more about HoyUltra 2000M SOURCE Hoymiles Power Electronics Inc.

artigo.texto: Novo aviso foi publicado nesta quarta-feira (30) e prevê contratação de empresa para diagnóstico da infraestrutura de tecnologia da informação; recentemente, a pasta também abriu dispensa para aquisição de uniformes A Secretaria Especial de Governo de Parauapebas (Segov) publicou nesta quarta-feira (30) mais um aviso de dispensa de licitação, ampliando a sequência de contratações diretas realizadas pela pasta. Desta vez, a Segov pretende contratar uma empresa especializada para realizar serviços técnicos de avaliação e diagnóstico da infraestrutura de tecnologia da informação do Data Center da secretaria. O valor global estimado da contratação é de R$ 64.966,32. Mais uma dispensa O novo procedimento é a Dispensa de Licitação de Valor nº 016/2026 e foi publicado no Diário Oficial desta quarta-feira. A publicação ocorre pouco tempo depois de outra contratação por dispensa envolvendo a Segov, desta vez para a aquisição de uniformes, procedimento que também foi noticiado pelo Portal Pebinha de Açúcar. Agora, a demanda é voltada à área de tecnologia. De acordo com o aviso, o serviço deverá contemplar a avaliação e o diagnóstico da infraestrutura de TI existente no Data Center da Secretaria Especial de Governo. O documento publicado, no entanto, apresenta apenas uma descrição resumida do objeto. Os detalhes técnicos, etapas do diagnóstico e demais exigências para a empresa contratada constam do processo e do edital correspondente. Menor preço global Apesar de se tratar de uma dispensa de licitação, empresas interessadas poderão apresentar propostas para disputar a contratação. Segundo o aviso, o critério adotado será o de menor preço global. O prazo para apresentação das propostas e da documentação termina às 14h do dia 5 de outubro de 2026. O valor de R$ 64,9 mil divulgado pela Segov é uma estimativa, portanto não significa necessariamente que esse será o montante efetivamente contratado. O valor final dependerá do resultado do procedimento. Contratação direta é prevista em lei A Segov fundamentou o procedimento no artigo 75, inciso II, da Lei Federal nº 14.133/2021, a Nova Lei de Licitações e Contratos Administrativos. Esse dispositivo permite, observados os requisitos legais e os limites de valor vigentes, a contratação direta para determinados serviços e compras. Portanto, a utilização de uma dispensa de licitação, por si só, não significa irregularidade. Mesmo nesses casos, a administração pública precisa justificar a contratação, observar os requisitos previstos em lei e dar publicidade ao procedimento. O aviso é assinado por Leonardo de Medeiros, da Secretaria Especial de Governo, e foi publicado em Parauapebas nesta quarta-feira, 30 de setembro.

artigo.texto: Falta de baterias faz Stellantis paralisar três fábricas na França por até duas semanas As unidades de Sochaux, de Rennes e de Mulhouse são as atingidas pela decisão A Stellantis vai paralisar a produção em três de suas fábricas na França por pelo menos uma semana, anunciou a montadora, movimento provocado em parte pela escassez de baterias para veículos elétricos. A unidade de Sochaux, no leste francês, responsável pela fabricação dos utilitários esportivos (SUVs) Peugeot 3008 e Peugeot 5008, interromperá as atividades entre 23 e 30 de outubro diante da oferta insuficiente de baterias de longo alcance, informou a companhia, em comunicado. A montadora justificou a decisão afirmando que a demanda por essas configurações segue forte, especialmente entre frotas corporativas, e continua superando a atual capacidade de fornecimento, tornando necessário um ajuste temporário no cronograma fabril para alinhar a produção à demanda do mercado e evitar a formação de estoques descalibrados, classificando a medida como pontual. A fábrica de Rennes também suspenderá as operações de 22 a 30 de outubro pelo mesmo motivo, com o gargalo de suprimentos afetando de forma mais acentuada a produção do Citroën C5 Aircross. A montadora adquire as baterias de longo alcance da Automotive Cells Co (ACC), empresa conjunta mantida em sociedade com a Mercedes-Benz e a TotalEnergies. A fabricante de componentes possui uma instalação na França, mas engavetou projetos para erguer complexos na Itália e na Alemanha nos últimos anos em razão do desaquecimento na procura por elétricos, mercado que voltou a se reaquecer neste ano, impulsionado pelo encarecimento dos combustíveis fósseis após a eclosão do conflito no Irã. Embora um porta-voz da Stellantis tenha afirmado que o ritmo de entrega de baterias ainda é insuficiente, a ACC declarou que o volume produzido em suas linhas em setembro deve se equiparar à produção de todo o ano de 2025, sustentando que os processos de industrialização e ganho de escala estão em andamento e atendem aos compromissos contratados com a montadora. Em paralelo, a fábrica de Mulhouse também interromperá os trabalhos entre 15 e 30 de outubro, por razões não relacionadas à cadeia de baterias. As paralisações nos três locais somam-se a uma suspensão de duas semanas programada para o fim de outubro no complexo fabril de Mirafiori, em Turim (Itália), onde os funcionários entrarão em regime de suspensão temporária de contrato. A unidade italiana já havia enfrentado interrupções operacionais em agosto e setembro, atribuídas formalmente à falta de componentes para motores, embora representações sindicais apontem para um ritmo de vendas inferior ao projetado para o modelo urbano Fiat 500 montado no local.

Summary As demand for AI, cloud computing and digital infrastructure accelerates, data center projects are growing in size and complexity, while facing increasing pressure to bring new capacity online as quickly as possible. Join Sherwin-Williams experts for a discussion on the evolving role of high-performance coatings in data center design and construction. artigo.texto: Pune: COEP Technological University and JSW Projects have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to set up what they describe as Indiaâs first indigenous battery prototyping and pilot-scale research and development centre at the universityâs Chikhali Research Park, with an investment of over Rs 800 crore across two phases. The centre will focus on developing and testing lithium-ion battery cells, along with sodium-ion and other advanced battery technologies. The initiative is expected to create over 1,000 jobs linked to the battery ecosystem and provide a platform for students and faculty to work with industry engineers on commercially relevant technologies. In the first phase, the centre will undertake battery-cell design, simulation and prototyping. The second phase will establish a cell validation facility with the capability to manufacture cells with capacities ranging from 100 to 600 Ah. COEP vice-chancellor Prof Sunil Bhirud said the partnership could help develop indigenous alternatives to imported batteries while giving students hands-on exposure to advanced battery technology. JSW Group chairman Sajjan Jindal said the partnership would help develop cells suited to Indian climatic conditions and applications. âCells are the new fuel of this century,â he said, and added that India needed to build domestic capabilities to manufacture them. The project aims to bridge the gap between academic research and industry by enabling joint research, technology development, publications and intellectual property creation. The centre is also expected to support applications in electric vehicles , grid storage and clean energy.

artigo.texto: As large-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in India move into the construction and delivery phase, the country’s domestic storage supply chain is expanding beyond project development into equipment manufacturing. Since the beginning of 2026, companies including JSW Energy, GoodEnough Energy and Waaree have brought GWh-scale BESS manufacturing and system integration capacity online, while Reliance and Vikram Solar are advancing larger battery and energy storage manufacturing projects. The shift is gradually changing India’s BESS supply model. Rather than relying heavily on imported complete systems, the market is increasingly moving toward a model in which cells and some key components are imported, while battery packs and system integration are completed locally. JSW Energy’s 5 GWh battery assembly facility in Pune, Maharashtra, is one of the most prominent examples of this transition. According to the company’s FY2025-26 annual report, its 5 GWh Battery Container Assembly Plant has commenced operations in Pune, marking JSW’s expansion from energy storage project investment and operation into equipment manufacturing. More importantly, the capacity is not being used solely to support JSW’s internal storage portfolio. In July 2026, JSW Energy subsidiary JSW Energy PSP Eleven secured an order from Bondada Renewable Energy to supply a 200 MW/400 MWh BESS together with power conversion systems (PCS). The contract was valued at approximately Rs 4.44 billion. The order indicates that JSW is beginning to compete in the third-party BESS equipment market, with its 5 GWh facility evolving from an internal supply-chain asset into a commercial storage manufacturing platform. Local BESS Integration Capacity Ramps Up JSW is not alone. Several GWh-scale BESS manufacturing and assembly facilities have emerged across India. Tata AutoComp Gotion Green Energy Solutions, the joint venture between Tata AutoComp and Gotion, has established 6 GWh of BESS manufacturing capacity and has begun supplying storage systems to Tata Power. GoodEnough Energy commissioned a 7 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in Noida in January 2026, while Waaree Energy Storage Solutions started operations at a 5.15 GWh automated BESS container manufacturing facility in Gujarat in July. Together with JSW’s 5 GWh plant, these four companies alone represent approximately 23.15 GWh/year of publicly disclosed BESS manufacturing and assembly capacity that has already been commissioned or brought into operation. India’s incumbent battery manufacturers are also expanding into lithium-ion battery packs and stationary storage. Amara Raja has commissioned the first 1.5 GWh phase of its battery pack facility in Telangana, with long-term pack capacity planned at 5 GWh to serve both electric vehicles and stationary energy storage. The company is also developing up to 16 GWh of upstream cell manufacturing capacity. Exide currently operates 1.5 GWh of lithium-ion module and pack capacity and, through Exide Energy Solutions, is developing a lithium-ion cell manufacturing complex in Bengaluru with planned capacity of up to 12 GWh. The prospective capacity pipeline is significantly larger. Reliance has said its BESS Gigafactory in Jamnagar has entered advanced commissioning. The facility is designed for 40 GWh/year of capacity and is expected to begin ramping up in the second half of 2026, with the company’s longer-term roadmap targeting 100 GWh. VSL PowerHive, a subsidiary of Vikram Solar, plans to establish 5 GWh of BESS manufacturing capacity in FY2027 and subsequently expand further into battery cell manufacturing. Powertrac, meanwhile, announced in August 2026 that it would develop a 10 GWh energy storage manufacturing facility in Ahmedabad covering both cell-to-pack and pack-to-container production. These figures should not be added together indiscriminately, as they include operating assembly capacity, projects under construction and longer-term cell manufacturing plans. Nevertheless, the overall direction is clear: India’s BESS manufacturing industry is moving from relatively fragmented project-level integration toward GWh-scale industrial production, with battery packs, containers and system integration currently leading the capacity build-out. “Made in India” BESS Does Not Yet Mean a Fully Localised Supply Chain The rapid expansion in pack and container assembly contrasts with much slower localisation of battery cells and some other critical components. Tata Power has said that India currently imports more than 80% of its battery cells. Until meaningful domestic cell capacity becomes available, the more practical supply-chain model remains importing cells and some key components, including certain BMS products, while completing racks, EMS, containers and system integration in India. The gap is consistent with the progress of India’s domestic cell manufacturing industry. The Indian government’s Advanced Chemistry Cell Production Linked Incentive (ACC PLI) scheme targets 50 GWh of advanced cell manufacturing capacity. By the end of 2025, 40 GWh had been awarded, but relatively little large-scale commercial production had materialised. India’s Ministry of Heavy Industries said in February 2026 that Ola had established approximately 1 GWh of ACC manufacturing capacity by the end of 2025 and was in the process of stabilising production, while other major PLI-backed projects remained under development or in the capacity ramp-up phase. Reliance, Amara Raja and Exide are expected to move progressively into construction, commissioning or commercial production windows during 2026-27. Amara Raja, for example, commissioned its Customer Qualification Plant in July 2026 and plans to establish its first 2 GWh of commercial cell manufacturing capacity in 2027. artigo.texto: Glencore International AG Major vanadium producer via ferrovanadium and V2O5 According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Vanadium Pentoxide Powder market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global vanadium pentoxide powder market is entering a phase of renewed demand expansion, with consumption projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 5–7% through 2035. This acceleration is primarily driven by two converging forces: the rapid deployment of vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, and the increasing use of vanadium pentoxide powder as a cathode dopant in lithium-ion batteries to enhance thermal stability and cycle life. Supply remains heavily concentrated, with China accounting for an estimated 55–65% of global production, followed by South Africa and Russia. This concentration creates structural import dependence in North America, Europe, and parts of Asia, exposing buyers to geopolitical and logistical risks. Prices for standard-grade material traded in a band of approximately $10–15/kg over 2023–2025, while high-purity grades command a 30–60% premium. As end users increasingly specify controlled particle size and minimal impurities, the share of premium grades is expected to rise from roughly 25% of tonnage in 2025 to 35–40% by 2035. This report provides a data-driven outlook on market size, demand architecture, supply dynamics, trade flows, pricing, and competitive landscape, offering a consistent analytical frame for strategic planning through 2035. The baseline scenario for the vanadium pentoxide powder market anticipates steady to accelerating growth over the 2026–2035 forecast period, with global consumption expanding at a CAGR of 5–7%. This outlook assumes no major supply disruptions beyond typical geopolitical frictions and a continued policy push for renewable energy integration and grid resilience. Demand-side fundamentals are strengthening: grid-scale energy storage installations are rising globally, and VRFBs are gaining traction due to their long duration, scalability, and safety. Simultaneously, lithium-ion battery manufacturers are increasingly adopting vanadium pentoxide as a dopant to improve cathode stability, particularly in high-nickel chemistries. On the supply side, production remains a co-product of steel slag processing, tying availability to steel market cycles. China's dominance in production and processing is expected to persist, though new conversion plants in North America, Australia, and Europe may gradually diversify supply after 2030. Price volatility is likely to continue, with a moderate upward bias as specialty demand tightens the market for high-purity grades. The market index (2025=100) is projected to reach 165 by 2035, reflecting cumulative growth. Key risks include regulatory compliance costs, trade barriers, and substitution in some applications, but the overall trajectory remains positive. The energy storage sector, particularly vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs), is the fastest-growing end use for vanadium pentoxide powder. VRFBs are increasingly favored for grid-scale storage due to their long duration, scalability, and ability to decouple power and energy capacity. Vanadium pentoxide powder is a key precursor for vanadium electrolyte, which is the active material in VRFB systems. As renewable energy penetration rises, utilities and independent power producers are investing in large-scale storage projects, driving demand for vanadium electrolyte. Demand-side indicators include grid storage capacity additions, renewable energy curtailment rates, and policy mandates for storage. Through 2035, VRFB deployments are expected to accelerate, especially in China, the US, and Europe, supported by declining system costs and growing familiarity with the technology. This segment is projected to increase its share of total vanadium pentoxide powder consumption from around 25% in 2025 to 35% by 2035. Current trend: Rapid growth. Major trends: Increasing project sizes for VRFB installations, with durations exceeding 4 hours, Vertical integration by battery manufacturers securing vanadium supply through long-term contracts, Development of next-generation VRFB chemistries with higher energy density and lower cost, Government auctions and incentives for long-duration storage in key markets, and Growing interest in vanadium electrolyte leasing models to reduce upfront costs. Representative participants: Rongke Power, Sumitomo Electric Industries, Invinity Energy Systems, Stryten Energy, VRB Energy, and Largo Inc. Vanadium pentoxide powder is used as a dopant in lithium-ion battery cathodes, particularly in high-nickel chemistries like NMC and NCA, to enhance thermal stability and extend cycle life. As electric vehicle (EV) adoption grows and battery manufacturers push for higher energy densities, the need for dopants that improve safety and longevity becomes critical. Vanadium doping helps stabilize the crystal structure of cathode materials, reducing degradation during charge-discharge cycles. Demand-side indicators include EV production volumes, battery energy density targets, and safety regulations. Through 2035, this segment is expected to grow steadily, driven by the expansion of the EV market and the increasing use of high-nickel cathodes. However, the share of vanadium pentoxide used for doping may be partially offset by alternative dopants or cathode chemistries, but overall volume is projected to rise. This segment is estimated to account for 25% of consumption in 2035. Current trend: Strong growth. artigo.texto: BYD Bets on Solid-State Batteries and Australian Hybrid Push as Shares Sit 30% Below Peak Published on 09/28/2026 at 14:02 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD is running two playbooks at once. On one side, the Chinese automaker is laying out a long-range technology roadmap that reaches into the next decade. On the other, it is moving aggressively into overseas showrooms with new hybrid and electric variants priced to undercut rivals. Investors, for now, are unimpressed: the stock changed hands at EUR 8.73 on the day of the Australian launch announcement, down 1.1%, and slipped a further 1.6% to EUR 8.70 as the battery plans were unveiled. Either way, the shares sit roughly 30% below their 52-week high of EUR 12.49. A Solid-State Timeline Set for Around 2030 Management has put a date on its next-generation battery ambitions. Mass commercial production of solid-state cells is targeted for the period around 2030, with sulfide-based solid electrolytes forming the backbone of the development effort. Chief scientist Lian Yubo made clear the new chemistry will not simply replace the existing Blade battery, which relies on lithium iron phosphate. The two are expected to run side by side, with solid-state packs reserved for premium models for the time being. That puts BYD on a similar footing with overseas competitors such as Toyota, which is also aiming for its first solid-state vehicles in 2027 and 2028. Bestsellers Get a Ground-Up Rework Alongside the battery roadmap, BYD pulled the wraps off heavily revised versions of two of its highest-volume nameplates for the home market. The Seagull city car — sold abroad as the Atto 1 — moves to a second generation built on a rear-wheel-drive platform with a multi-link rear suspension. It seats five, and its electric motor now produces 95 kilowatts. A Chinese market launch is planned before the end of 2026. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? The second-generation Seal 07 sedan was also previewed with official images and specifications. It grows noticeably in both length and wheelbase. Buyers will be able to choose between a plug-in hybrid variant and a fully electric version whose motor delivers up to 300 kilowatts. A roof-mounted LiDAR system is among the options, enabling more advanced driver-assistance functions. Australia Becomes a Testbed for Plug-In Hybrids The overseas offensive is most visible Down Under, where BYD has introduced the Atto 2 DM-i compact SUV. The entry-level Essential trim starts at AUD 24,990 before on-road costs, pairing a 1.5-litre petrol engine with a 7.85-kilowatt-hour battery for 39 kilometres of WLTP electric-only range. Total range is quoted at 845 kilometres. The Premium grade asks AUD 29,990 and uses an 18.03-kilowatt-hour LFP pack good for 90 electric kilometres. Sajid Hasan, BYD Australia's product chief, told CarExpert the vehicle faces no direct plug-in hybrid competitors in its segment. The lineup is rounded out by a refreshed Atto 3 EVO, which opens at AUD 41,990 as the Dynamic variant. The Premium version, at AUD 46,990, runs an 800-volt system capable of 220-kilowatt DC charging, enough to go from 10% to 80% in roughly 25 minutes. Fleet Sales Climb as Exports Fill the Gap Commercial buyers have become a bigger part of the Australian story. Chief operating officer Stephen Collins said the company's fleet share of the local sales mix jumped from 7% to 8% a year ago to 20% today, with a medium-term target of the mid-30% range. That overseas momentum matters because the domestic picture is tougher. BYD exported 173,721 new-energy vehicles in July, according to data from Chinese industry association PCA, while total vehicle sales for the month rose 22% to about 420,000 units. The pressure at home is stark: sales of conventional combustion cars in China fell 41% in July even as the country's overall auto exports surged 88%. To shore up its position outside Asia, BYD is pressing ahead with European projects, including the expansion of its own plant in Szeged, Hungary. A Recall and a Security Probe Add Friction Not everything is running smoothly. BYD Australia confirmed an internal investigation into a media report alleging unauthorised remote access to a Shark 6 pickup. Teams in Australia and China are involved. The manufacturer says personal data belonging to local customers is stored on Australian servers. Separately, a local recall of the pickup is under way over a potentially faulty spare-wheel mounting. artigo.texto: A operadora de eventos Informa Markets anunciou a realização da edição 2026 do Futurecom, agendada para ocorrer entre 6 e 8 de outubro no pavilhão do São Paulo Expo, na capital paulista. De acordo com a entidade organizadora, a convenção deste ano projeta reunir um público superior a 30 mil visitantes, além de 300 marcas expositoras e cerca de 400 palestrantes distribuídos ao longo de 93 horas de conteúdo. O encontro pretende debater a convergência entre modelos avançados de inteligência artificial, redes de telecomunicações, segurança digital e a demanda por infraestrutura pesada de processamento. Segundo o material divulgado pela promotora, a solenidade de abertura terá a participação institucional do Ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Siqueira, que deve abordar os planos governamentais voltados à expansão da conectividade em território nacional e as diretrizes regulatórias para os serviços digitais. A entidade remetente sustenta que a edição foi reestruturada para consolidar frentes operacionais que historicamente caminhavam apartadas, congregando fornecedores de conectividade, operadores de sistemas de nuvem, gestores de energia e desenvolvedores de aplicações para o ecossistema corporativo e governamental. Reconfiguração do ecossistema e demandas de infraestrutura setorial O setor de tecnologia da informação e comunicações (TIC) no Brasil opera sob a pressão de coordenar a expansão das redes 5G com a iminência de pesquisas voltadas ao padrão 6G, além da necessidade premente de modernizar as redes industriais e os parques legados. Conforme a Informa Markets, a separação tradicional entre empresas de telecomunicações e provedores de serviços digitais deixou de refletir a dinâmica de mercado, demandando modelos operacionais conjuntos entre operadoras de rede móvel, operadoras neutras e provedores de serviços de internet (ISPs). A concentração dos grandes polos de transmissão de dados na Região Metropolitana de São Paulo expõe desafios contínuos em termos de capacidade energética, licenciamento de antenas e infraestrutura de fibras ópticas de alta vazão. Dados da organização do evento indicam que a nova configuração temática visa oferecer às lideranças empresariais subsídios para lidar com os gargalos estruturais das cadeias de suprimentos, carência de componentes especializados e os limites físicos impostos pelas redes metropolitanas de distribuição elétrica. A tabela abaixo sintetiza a distribuição estrutural dos espaços temáticos anunciados para a feira de negócios e congresso: Convergência entre modelos de inteligência artificial e capacidade computacional Conforme destaca a Informa Markets, a programação congressual passa a adotar a denominação de Futurecom Leaders Congress, estruturada em cinco palcos distintos. A organização alega que a grade abordará desde o uso corporativo de agentes autônomos e governança de dados até a implantação de redes móveis privativas em verticais intensivas como agronegócio, manufatura, logística, mineração e saúde digital. O executivo Fernando D’Ascola, Head de Infra e Tech Business da organizadora, afirma na divulgação que a reestruturação acompanha a exigência de integrar inteligência computacional, matriz energética, centros de processamento e telecomunicações. No campo acadêmico e técnico, o comunicado aponta que a pesquisadora brasileira Elisa Pereira, da Universidade de Stanford, apresentará conclusões de um levantamento sobre implementação de ferramentas de inteligência artificial. De acordo com os dados reportados, 77% dos entraves centrais para a maturação dessas iniciativas residem em processos organizacionais, incentivos corporativos e gestão comportamental, sobrepondo-se aos desafios estritamente tecnológicos. Em paralelo, a agenda inclui o seminário Quantum for Business Leaders, conduzido pelo cientista Paulo Sergio Rufino Henrique, focado na transição para algoritmos de criptografia pós-quântica e protocolos de defesa cibernética para sistemas autônomos. A programação também contempla conferências sobre liderança e resiliência ministradas pelo atleta olímpico Cesar Cielo e pela ex-ginasta Laís Souza. Segundo a organizadora, os palestrantes abordarão a correlação entre execução técnica, acessibilidade e superação de limites operacionais em organizações de alta complexidade. Demonstrações operacionais e expansão da cadeia de valor em hardware A entidade promotora afirma que o espaço de exposição apresentará tecnologias aplicadas que demandam transmissão em tempo real e sensoriamento avançado. Entre as inovações selecionadas para exibição no São Paulo Expo, constam: - Robôs autônomos quadrúpedes interligados por modems e enlaces 5G voltados a inspeções industriais em ambientes de risco; - Espelho inteligente dotado de módulos de visão computacional e algoritmos de inteligência artificial destinados a aferir frequência cardíaca, ritmo respiratório e oxigenação sanguínea sem contato epidérmico direto; - Agentes de inteligência artificial generativa configurados para atuar na esteira de atendimento ao cliente, automação de fluxos de trabalho corporativos e integração instantânea a sistemas de gestão e CRM; - Conjuntos ópticos portáteis concebidos para diagnosticar, auditar e mapear parâmetros físicos de redes de fibra óptica de forma remota; - Tecnologias de borda (edge computing) focadas em transferir o processamento de modelos analíticos diretamente para o ponto de coleta de dados em plantas fabris. Paralelamente, o comunicado ressalta a realização concomitante da primeira edição do evento Data Center World Brasil no mesmo complexo. artigo.texto: DCF Trends Summit: ON.energy’s Asser Elsamahy - Using AI UPS Systems to Tame AI Load Swings Key Highlights - Battery systems are being adapted for AI data centers to handle rapid workload changes without stressing the electric grid. - The AI UPS architecture uses dual inverters to separate grid requirements from data center load demands, improving power stability and compliance. - Batteries can be recharged during off-peak times or through AI load fluctuations, acting as reservoirs of energy to buffer demand swings. - Energy storage enables data centers to reduce their grid draw during peak stress, helping stabilize the overall electrical system. - As AI loads grow, stricter grid requirements like voltage and frequency ride-through are prompting data centers to incorporate advanced power quality solutions. The power challenge surrounding artificial intelligence is increasingly about more than finding enough megawatts. AI data centers can also introduce rapid changes in electricity demand as large clusters of accelerators ramp workloads up and down. Those swings create a different kind of infrastructure problem: how to serve highly dynamic compute loads without passing that volatility directly onto the electric grid. That challenge is helping move battery energy storage deeper into data center power architecture. In an onsite podcast interview recorded live at the Data Center Frontier Trends Summit 2026, DCF Contributing Editor Doug Black spoke with Asser Elsamahy, P.E., vice president of engineering at ON.energy, about the emerging role of battery-based power quality infrastructure for AI data centers. Elsamahy said battery power systems themselves are hardly new. Energy storage has been deployed at gigawatt scale around the world for roughly two decades. What is new is the way the technology is being adapted to the operating characteristics of large AI facilities. “They’re new to the data center industry, but they’re not necessarily new in the market,” Elsamahy said. “They’ve been deployed at gigawatt scale already, multiple gigawatts all over the world.” The difference now is the load. Major swings in AI computing demand can create additional stress for grid operators already confronting rapid growth in large-load interconnection requests. Elsamahy said that dynamic is accelerating interest in energy storage as a way to manage the interface between AI infrastructure and the grid. From Battery Storage to an “AI UPS” ON.energy’s approach is built around what the company calls an AI UPS, or medium-voltage uninterruptible power supply. The architecture differs from the parallel battery energy storage system, or BESS, configuration commonly used for standalone grid storage. ON instead uses a double-conversion design with two sets of inverters. One inverter set faces the grid and can respond to utility or grid-operator requirements. Those requirements can include voltage ride-through, frequency behavior and limits on how rapidly a large facility ramps power consumption. The second inverter set faces the data center load. That allows the load-facing system to deliver the power demanded by the computing environment — including peaks, surges and rapid changes — while the grid-facing side behaves according to the requirements of the utility system. The result, according to Elsamahy, is a degree of electrical separation between what happens inside the AI data center and what is presented to the grid. “You have two sets of inverters,” he said. “One set that’s connected to the grid does what the grid wants, follows the grid requirements.” The other, he continued, is “facing the load” and supplies what that load demands. That distinction becomes particularly important when compared with a conventional parallel BESS architecture using a single set of inverters. With one inverter interface, Elsamahy said, the storage system can face competing requirements from the data center and the grid. “It kind of is in a constant struggle of, do I support the grid or do I support the load?” he said. “I have to pick one or the other. It’s very difficult to do both.” For data center designers, that points toward a larger change in how batteries may be considered in future AI facilities. Rather than serving primarily as stored energy for backup operation or standalone grid services, batteries can become part of the facility’s power-quality architecture — shaping the electrical behavior of the data center itself. Using AI’s Load Swings to Recharge Any architecture that routinely draws from batteries must also manage state of charge. Elsamahy described two ways the system can replenish stored energy. The first is straightforward: during favorable operating periods, the data center can draw slightly more power from the grid than the compute load itself requires, directing the excess into the batteries. For a hypothetical 1-gigawatt load, for example, the facility might draw modestly above 1 GW when grid conditions and electricity pricing make doing so advantageous. “Typically you do that during off-peak, when energy price … is usually the lowest,” Elsamahy said. But the variability of the AI load itself can also provide charging opportunities. Because compute demand naturally rises and falls, the battery system can absorb energy during downward portions of that load profile and discharge when demand rises again. “That’s kind of the beauty of the batteries,” Elsamahy said. “It’s basically a reservoir of energy.” The concept effectively turns battery storage into a buffer between two environments with very different preferences: AI infrastructure that can change power demand abruptly, and an electric grid that operates most reliably when large loads behave predictably. A New Meaning for “Grid Citizen” That buffering capability also intersects with one of the industry’s most difficult emerging issues: how rapidly growing data center loads affect utilities and surrounding communities. artigo.texto: Juniper Green Energy Limited, through its wholly owned subsidiary Juniper Green Cosmic Private Limited, has commissioned an additional 100 MWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity at its Bikaner-II project in Rajasthan, increasing the project’s total commissioned storage capacity from 101 MWh to 201 MWh. The additional BESS capacity has been commissioned within the project’s existing grid connectivity, following regulatory clarity issued by the Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (CTUIL). The framework allows storage capacity to be added without increasing the grid connectivity quantum, enabling greater utilisation of existing transmission infrastructure. Juniper Green Energy said the approach allows it to add incremental storage capacity in a capital-efficient manner. The newly commissioned capacity will initially operate on a merchant basis, allowing the company to participate in India’s developing energy storage market and capture opportunities arising from growing demand for grid flexibility and balancing services. The commissioning forms part of Juniper Green Energy’s strategy to develop a diversified portfolio of renewable energy and energy storage assets, combining its long-term contracted portfolio with merchant revenue opportunities. The company said it plans to continue expanding its BESS capabilities as India’s electricity system increasingly requires flexible energy storage solutions to support the integration of growing renewable energy capacity. Ankush Malik, Whole-time Director and CEO of Juniper Green Energy, said the additional capacity demonstrates the company’s strategy of maximising the value of existing infrastructure. He added that increasing Bikaner-II’s commissioned storage capacity to 201 MWh creates additional merchant capacity without requiring incremental grid connectivity. The development further strengthens Juniper Green Energy’s energy storage portfolio as the company looks to build greater commercial flexibility alongside its contracted renewable energy assets. artigo.texto: Volkswagen is betting on a closer partnership with China's Gotion in the field of batteries. According to Automobilwoche, the automaker intends to expand the European production of relatively inexpensive lithium-iron-phosphate cells and thereby reduce dependence on third-party suppliers. Cooperation will develop in several directions at once. Gotion will receive a share in the PowerCo plant in Sagunto in Spain, where it is planned to produce batteries. In addition, the companies will jointly manage an enterprise for the production of cells in Surany in Slovakia and a cathode materials plant in Kenitra in Morocco. Under the terms of the deal, Gotion will invest 1.1 billion euros in the Spanish project. Volkswagen, in turn, will invest 470 million euros in joint ventures in Slovakia and Morocco. PowerCo will retain 51% of the Spanish plant and 49% each in the other two companies. The partnership will be based on LFP technology. It is considered cheaper, safer and more durable than NMC chemistry, although it is inferior to it in terms of energy density. For Volkswagen, this is an important step towards more affordable electric vehicles, as it is these batteries that are planned to be used in new mass models. Production in Valencia is scheduled to start next year. Batteries from this facility are expected to be supplied for Volkswagen ID models. Polo and ID. Cross, as well as for Škoda Epiq and Cupra Raval. The partners are not limited to LFP batteries only. PowerCo and Gotion are also working on sodium-ion and solid-state technologies that could form the basis for next-generation batteries. At the same time, Volkswagen will reduce its direct stake in Gotion from 24% to 19%. The concern expects that such a scheme will allow PowerCo to become more technologically independent, but it will not require too much investment at the start. At the same time, dependence on Chinese expertise will remain. PowerCo continues to look for new investors and may enter the stock exchange in the future. However, the company must first prove that it is capable of establishing profitable mass production of battery cells in Europe.

artigo.texto: LG Electronics lança Chiller Centrífugo Refrigerado a Ar para data centers de IA AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 28 de setembro de 2026 Empresa expande portfólio de resfriamento para data centers de IA com soluções confiáveis e de alta eficiência baseadas em tecnologias proprietárias Resumo da notícia - A LG Electronics lança seu Chiller Centrífugo Refrigerado a Ar (ACC) de alta eficiência e alta confiabilidade, projetado para atender à crescente demanda de resfriamento de data centers de IA (AIDCs). - O chiller conta com tecnologias proprietárias Core Tech da LG, incluindo compressor com mancal magnético livre de óleo e tecnologia inovadora de free-cooling por refrigerante. - Em caso de interrupção de energia, o chiller pode restaurar a capacidade total de resfriamento em até 3 minutos após o restabelecimento da energia, protegendo a continuidade operacional.³ - A solução modular de resfriamento hidrônico da LG simplifica a instalação no local por meio de pré-fabricação e montagem em fábrica, enquanto o design modular do chiller oferece flexibilidade para expansão rápida e escalável da capacidade dos AIDCs. SÃO PAULO, Brazil, Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — A LG Electronics (LG) lança seu Chiller Centrífugo Refrigerado a Ar (ACC) de alta eficiência e alta confiabilidade para atender à crescente demanda de resfriamento de data centers de IA (AIDCs). A solução foi projetada para melhorar o desempenho energético e manter a continuidade do resfriamento, fortalecendo ainda mais o portfólio de resfriamento de data centers da empresa. Disponível de 480 a 600 toneladas de refrigeração (RT) por unidade, o chiller pode ser configurado para AIDCs com diferentes necessidades de resfriamento.¹ Resfriamento de alta eficiência com tecnologias avançadas No núcleo do novo Chiller Centrífugo Refrigerado a Ar da LG está um compressor centrífugo com mancal magnético livre de óleo. Ao usar força magnética para suspender o eixo rotativo sem contato físico, o design elimina a necessidade de óleo lubrificante, reduzindo perdas por atrito mecânico e melhorando o desempenho de compressão. O chiller também incorpora tecnologia de free-cooling por refrigerante, utilizando o ar externo frio para reduzir a carga de resfriamento do compressor. Diferentemente dos sistemas convencionais de free-cooling, ele circula o refrigerante diretamente, sem um trocador de calor intermediário, e não requer glicol, minimizando perdas de calor e pressão e simplificando a manutenção. Com base em simulação interna da LG, o free-cooling por refrigerante pode consumir aproximadamente 30% menos energia por ano do que o free-cooling hidrônico.² Além disso, a tecnologia de fluxo contracorrente em série (SCF) da LG ajuda a manter a operação equilibrada ao distribuir a carga de resfriamento entre os compressores. Operação confiável e gestão flexível Além de melhorar a eficiência energética, o chiller foi projetado para oferecer resfriamento consistente e operações confiáveis em AIDCs. Seu sensor de gap, integrado ao sistema de mancal magnético, detecta com precisão o eixo de rotação para permitir um controle preciso. Recursos de machine learning permitem que o chiller se adapte a padrões de operação, ajudando a reduzir instabilidades operacionais. Durante uma interrupção de energia, um sistema de alimentação ininterrupta (UPS) integrado fornece energia de emergência, permitindo que o eixo pare com segurança e reduzindo o potencial de danos ao mancal. O sistema também oferece um recurso de recuperação rápida, que restaura a capacidade de resfriamento em até 3 minutos após o restabelecimento da energia.³ A LG também está fortalecendo suas capacidades de controle e operação por meio do Data Center Cooling Management (DCCM). O software permite monitoramento integrado e controle orientado por dados em infraestruturas de resfriamento complexas, incluindo CDU (Coolant Distribution Unit), Computer Room Air Handler (CRAH) e Chiller Centrífugo Refrigerado a Ar. Ele contribui para uma gestão de risco mais sólida com manutenção preditiva, enquanto a otimização em tempo real baseada nas cargas de trabalho de TI pode melhorar a eficiência operacional. artigo.texto: The province of Chubut seeks to promote new sustainable financing tools to improve its competitiveness with the development of a carbon market. Governor Ignacio “Nacho” Torres outlined these objectives during the closing of “Carbono Chubut: valuing the ecosystem services of Patagonia“, a meeting that brought together public, scientific, academic, and productive leaders. A meeting focused on carbon capture The meeting analyzed strategies to reduce emissions, value ecosystem services, and generate economic instruments linked to carbon capture. The agenda included everything from the restoration of the native forest and fire prevention, to solar and wind energy, green hydrogen, biofuels, and regenerative livestock farming. Torres stated that environmental policy can be articulated with an economic development strategy. “This Congress is very important. We have a non-negotiable premise: facing climate change is not a barrier to development. We have a province with impressive diversity: forest, steppe, mountains, and sea. And we must take care of that diversity,” said the governor. Carbon credits as a financing tool One of the main focuses of the meeting was the potential of carbon credits as a financing tool. The goal is for projects capable of capturing carbon or reducing emissions to generate resources to sustain environmental and productive initiatives. “Fire prevention is a central issue for us. At the same time, we are working on restoration to replant our native forest. It will take time, but it must be a long-term state policy. And carbon credits are fundamental to financing these projects,” Torres noted. The governor also focused on carbon capture in soils and its potential economic impact. “It is very important to work on carbon capture in our soil. It is a huge opportunity, and we must promote it to be more competitive,” he stated. Chubut already has seven photovoltaic parks The provincial strategy also includes the growth of renewable energies. Torres indicated that Chubut currently has more than seven photovoltaic parks. He also highlighted the tax incentives aimed at the sector, along with the possibility for families, companies, and cooperatives to produce renewable energy and sell their surpluses. “Decarbonizing means measuring, reducing emissions, and gaining efficiency,” stated the leader, linking the energy transition with the need to support electro-intensive activities and a growing demand for electricity. A regulatory framework for the provincial carbon market Another objective is to move towards a provincial regulatory framework for the carbon market. Vice Governor Gustavo Menna noted that the debate developed during the meeting could contribute to promoting specific legislation in the Legislature. In fact, the legislative building itself has already incorporated 260 solar panels. As presented during the event, this system allows for a reduction of more than 23% in energy consumption from the grid. It also avoids the emission of about 118 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent per year. A plan aligned with the 2030 climate goals The Secretary of Environment and Sustainable Development Control, Juan José Rivera, explained that the initiative is part of the provincial Climate Change Response Plan. The work aims to identify decarbonization strategies for different activities and advance in the monetization of ecosystem services. Chubut also has specific regulations on methane emissions and works with the horizon of the goals set for 2030. Forest restoration, biochar, and sustainable livestock The event also addressed projects for the restoration of the Andean Forest, afforestation and reforestation, and the use of biochar to capture carbon and improve soils. Sustainable management alternatives for the steppe, grasslands, and sheep farming were also discussed. Additionally, the possibilities of green hydrogen, advanced biofuels, wind and solar energy were analyzed, along with tools to measure and verify emission reductions. The challenge posed by the province is to convert these environmental and energy capabilities into projects that can access financing and attract capital. Torres stated that the goal is to have rules that allow Chubut “to be competitive and a spearhead in an issue that the world demands today.”

artigo.texto: Volkswagen's PowerCo and Gotion to Invest €3.2B in Battery Joint Ventures Across Europe and Morocco Published: Sep 30, 2026 19:09 (GMT+8) Share Share Save Volkswagen Group announced on September 28 that its battery subsidiary PowerCo and Gotion High-Tech plan to establish three joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco, with total investment of about EUR 3.222 billion (EUR 1.598 billion from the Gotion side and EUR 1.624 billion from the PowerCo side). Valencia, Spain will host a 29.1 GWh-per-year cell project costing about EUR 2.262 billion, held 51 percent by PowerCo with the Gotion side injecting about EUR 1.1 billion for 49 percent. The Surany, Slovakia plant becomes an 8.4 GWh-per-year joint venture with about EUR 480 million of investment, 51 percent Gotion-owned, serving EV and battery storage applications. Kenitra, Morocco will add a plant producing 100,000 tonnes per year of LFP cathode material for about EUR 480 million, majority-owned by Gotion. LFP cells use copper foil as the anode current collector, so the combined 37.5 GWh of planned capacity will add to European local copper foil demand once commissioned. artigo.texto: New Delhi: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) has expanded its operational battery energy storage system capacity to 6.63 GWh, which can store enough clean energy to power around two million homes a day. With this, the company has achieved almost 70 per cent of the company's target for FY27. The 6.63 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS) supports peak electricity demand of cities like Nagpur, Patna or Vizag for several hours. Also read: Cabinet gives green signal to Green Energy Corridor III The company now accounts for more than 50 per cent of India's operational BESS capacity of about 12.6 GWh, AGEL said in a statement on Thursday. The Adani Group entity said it has achieved the 6.63 GWh milestone within 14 months of commencing on-site BESSconstruction at Khavda, and is on track to add over 10 GWh of BESS capacity in 2026-27. As of June 2026, AGEL had 3.55 GWh of operational BESS capacity. The company is targeting 50 GWh of storage capacity over the next 5 years. The BESS uses lithium-ion battery technology, integrated with an energy management systems (EMS) and automated telemetry to manage charging and discharging, optimise system performance and support grid services. A battery storage can improve grid stability, manage peak demand, reduce energy curtailment and enable renewable power to be delivered when required. Also read: 4 Adani group companies settle public shareholding violations case with Sebi. Check details The latest operational BESS capacity is integrated with the company's renewable energy (RE) development at Khavda, where the company is developing a 30 GW RE plant across 538 square kilometers of barren land. Sagar Adani, Executive Director, Adani Green Energy, said, reaching 6.63 GWh of operational battery storage in just 14 months is a significant milestone for AGEL and India's clean energy transition. "As India's power demand grows, we will continue to scale energy storage solutions, both, battery and pumped storage to support a more resilient, lower-carbon grid," he said. artigo.texto: Demanda de data centers assegura aumento da capacidade das termelétricas A estrutura dos afamados data centers exige fornecimento contínuo, estável e de confiabilidade superior a 99%, por isso, essas usinas vêm ganhando destaque Atualizado Projeções do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) apontam salto importante na capacidade instalada das termelétricas, que funcionam como uma espécie de “seguro” para suprir a demanda de energia em horários de pico, ou quando fontes intermitentes geram menos. A estimativa para os próximos anos é passar dos atuais 39.483 MW para 45.982 MW em 2030. O otimismo do setor vem não apenas do recente Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade (LRCAP 2026), que contratou 18.977 MW — entre novas termelétricas, as já existentes e ampliação de hidrelétricas —, mas também da antecipação de contratos que previam adicionar 1.678,4 MW ao Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) no início de setembro. Para 2027, o setor projeta nova expansão por meio de leilões de capacidade, segundo a Associação Brasileira de Geradoras Termelétricas (Abraget). Também impulsiona o setor a demanda de energia por data centers, que exigem fornecimento contínuo, estável e de confiabilidade superior a 99%. Por isso, termelétricas — especialmente as movidas a gás natural e biomassa — vêm ganhando destaque na segurança energética de infraestruturas críticas e do sistema elétrico nacional. Xisto Vieira Filho, presidente da Abraget, explica que o risco de déficit de oferta no setor elétrico para os próximos anos pode superar o limite de 5% estabelecido pelo Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE) em cenários de forte estresse hidrológico, períodos severos de seca ou alta demanda. “Essa projeção reforça a necessidade de novas termelétricas para garantir a segurança de suprimento”, diz. Estimulados por esse cenário, operadores vêm ampliando seus investimentos. A Mercurio Partners, por exemplo, está desembolsando R$ 1,4 bilhão na construção de cinco usinas termelétricas a gás natural em Alagoas (Pilar I, II, III, IV e V). Essas unidades, que venderam 241,63 MW no LRCAP 2026, serão implantadas em duas fases. A primeira, de 145,72 MW, para atendimento ao SIN a partir de outubro de 2028. Os outros 95,91 MW para atendimento a partir de agosto de 2029. “Os contratos têm prazo de 15 anos e vão gerar cerca de mil empregos diretos durante a construção”, informa Alexandre Americano, CEO da Mercurio Partners. Ele explica que o complexo de Pilar será composto de usinas 100% flexíveis, que, por sua modularidade tecnológica, poderão ser despachadas (acionadas) a qualquer momento pelo ONS. A Mercurio Partners também venceu a renovação do contrato da UTE Paulínia Verde (SP). Conectada à rede da Comgás, a usina de 23,4 MW retomou as operações em agosto. A Origem Energia investirá R$ 2 bilhões na construção de sete usinas termelétricas, também em Alagoas, onde já possui uma operação integrada de soluções energéticas baseadas no gás natural. Os projetos somam 372 MW de capacidade instalada. Pilar Nova (187 MW) e Pilar (135 MW) têm entrada em operação comercial prevista para outubro de 2028, enquanto as outras cinco usinas Manguaba, com 10 MW cada uma, estão previstas para agosto de 2029. “O diferencial importante desses projetos é sua configuração modular. As usinas serão constituídas por motores de 10 MW, cuja configuração permite ajustar a geração em diferentes patamares, adequando a potência entregue à demanda do ONS”, diz Carolina Szczerbacki, diretora de geração de energia da empresa. Segundo a executiva, esses projetos materializam a estratégia de integração gás-energia da empresa, agregando valor ao gás de produção própria e oferecendo ao sistema geração flexível e confiável. “A companhia tem apetite para ampliar sua capacidade termelétrica e pretende avaliar a participação nos próximos leilões de reserva de capacidade.” A Eneva, também vencedora no LRCAP, com 5,06 GW de capacidade contratada, deve investir R$ 18,2 bilhões em empreendimentos com início de operação previsto para 2028 até 2031. Os novos projetos — usinas termelétricas movidas a gás natural — estão concentrados em Sergipe, Ceará e região Sudeste do país. “Trata-se de empreendimentos estruturantes, integrados à infraestrutura de gás natural e localizados em regiões onde a Eneva já tem experiência operacional e presença consolidada”, diz Christiano Vieira, diretor-executivo de regulação do sistema elétrico da companhia. Segundo ele, a expansão inclui o Hub Sergipe (vencedor no produto 2028), com três novas usinas associadas a um terminal de GNL já operacional; o Hub Ceará (vencedor no produto 2030), que reúne duas usinas integradas a um novo terminal de GNL no porto de Pecém; e o Hub Sudeste (vencedor no produto 2031), formado por quatro usinas que utilizarão gás natural proveniente de uma nova infraestrutura de GNL . Sobre curtailment decorrente do excesso de geração, que impacta geradoras de energia solar e eólica, Vieira Filho, da Abraget, explica que as termelétricas estão muito menos expostas a esse tipo de restrição. Ainda assim, algumas térmicas podem ser impactadas, dependendo de sua localização elétrica. Americano, da Mercurio Partners, diz que fontes despacháveis não costumam sofrer curtailment, já que são ligadas exatamente para suprir a carga que renováveis não conseguem suprir.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de pó de pentóxido de vanádio: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de pó de pentóxido de vanádio até 2035: demanda acelera com armazenamento de energia em escala de rede e dopagem de cátodos Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de pó de pentóxido de vanádio, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de pó de pentóxido de vanádio entra em uma fase de renovada expansão da demanda, com o consumo projetado para crescer a uma taxa composta anual de 5% a 7% até 2035. Essa aceleração é impulsionada principalmente por duas forças convergentes: a rápida implantação de baterias de fluxo de vanádio (VRFBs) para armazenamento de energia em escala de rede e o uso crescente de pó de pentóxido de vanádio como dopante de cátodo em baterias de lithium-ion, para aumentar a estabilidade térmica e a vida útil dos ciclos. A oferta permanece fortemente concentrada, com a China respondendo por uma estimativa de 55% a 65% da produção global, seguida pela África do Sul e pela Rússia. Essa concentração cria dependência estrutural de importações na América do Norte, na Europa e em parte da Ásia, expondo os compradores a riscos geopolíticos e logísticos. Os preços do material de grau padrão foram negociados em uma faixa de aproximadamente US$ 10 a US$ 15/kg entre 2023 e 2025, enquanto os graus de alta pureza alcançam um prêmio de 30% a 60%. À medida que os usuários finais especificam cada vez mais tamanho de partícula controlado e impurezas mínimas, espera-se que a participação dos graus premium suba de cerca de 25% do volume em 2025 para 35% a 40% até 2035. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, arquitetura da demanda, dinâmica de oferta, fluxos comerciais, precificação e panorama competitivo, proporcionando um quadro analítico consistente para o planejamento estratégico até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de pó de pentóxido de vanádio prevê crescimento estável a acelerado no período de previsão de 2026 a 2035, com o consumo global avançando a uma taxa composta anual de 5% a 7%. Essa perspectiva pressupõe a ausência de grandes rupturas de oferta além das fricções geopolíticas típicas e a continuidade do impulso político à integração de energias renováveis e à resiliência da rede elétrica. Os fundamentos do lado da demanda estão se fortalecendo: as instalações de armazenamento de energia em escala de rede aumentam globalmente, e as VRFBs ganham tração por sua longa duração, escalabilidade e segurança. Ao mesmo tempo, fabricantes de baterias de lithium-ion adotam cada vez mais o pentóxido de vanádio como dopante para melhorar a estabilidade do cátodo, sobretudo em químicas de alto teor de níquel. Do lado da oferta, a produção continua sendo um coproduto do processamento de escória de aço, o que vincula a disponibilidade aos ciclos do mercado siderúrgico. Espera-se que o domínio da China na produção e no processamento persista, embora novas plantas de conversão na América do Norte, na Austrália e na Europa possam diversificar gradualmente a oferta após 2030. A volatilidade de preços provavelmente continuará, com leve viés de alta à medida que a demanda especializada aperta o mercado de graus de alta pureza. O índice de mercado (2025=100) deve alcançar 165 até 2035, refletindo o crescimento acumulado. Os principais riscos incluem custos de conformidade regulatória, barreiras comerciais e substituição em algumas aplicações, mas a trajetória geral permanece positiva. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores da Demanda - Aumento da implantação de baterias de fluxo de vanádio (VRFBs) para armazenamento de energia em escala de rede, impulsionado pela necessidade de armazenamento de longa duração e de integração de energias renováveis. - Uso crescente de pó de pentóxido de vanádio como dopante de cátodo em baterias de lithium-ion para aumentar a estabilidade térmica e a vida útil dos ciclos, especialmente em químicas de alto teor de níquel. - Demanda crescente por graus de alta pureza em aplicações especializadas, como catalisadores e síntese química, sustentada por especificações de qualidade mais rigorosas. - Políticas e incentivos governamentais que promovem o armazenamento de energia e os veículos elétricos, sobretudo na China, nos Estados Unidos e na Europa. - Expansão da produção de aço em mercados emergentes, o que amplia a disponibilidade de escória de vanádio como coproduto e sustenta indiretamente a oferta de pentóxido de vanádio. - Avanços tecnológicos na extração e no processamento de vanádio, que melhoram o rendimento e reduzem custos, tornando o pentóxido de vanádio mais acessível para aplicações em baterias. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Forte concentração da oferta na China, na África do Sul e na Rússia, expondo os compradores a riscos geopolíticos, controles de exportação e rupturas comerciais. - Custos de conformidade ambiental e regulatória associados ao processamento de vanádio, incluindo gestão de resíduos perigosos e controle de emissões, que elevam os custos de produção e atrasam nova capacidade. - Volatilidade de preços ligada aos ciclos do mercado siderúrgico, já que o vanádio é recuperado principalmente como coproduto da escória de aço, tornando oferta e preços sensíveis à demanda por aço. - Concorrência de tecnologias alternativas de armazenamento de energia, como baterias de lithium-ion e de sódio-enxofre, que pode limitar a adoção de VRFBs em algumas regiões. - Falta de especificações padronizadas e de certificação de qualidade para o pó de pentóxido

artigo.texto: China’s Gotion High-Tech wins 6GWh battery storage contracts in Saudi Arabia By Majda Muhsen China's Gotion High-Tech has secured contracts covering 6 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery energy storage capacity under Saudi Power Procurement Company's (SPPC) first group (G1) of utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) procurement programme. According to the company’s press statement, it secured Al Muwayah, Haden and Al Kahafa projects, each with a capacity of 500 megawatts (MW)/2gigawatt-hours (GWh), giving Gotion a combined capacity of 1.5GW/6GWh. The contracts mark the first large-scale international deployment of Gotion Grid, the company's utility-scale battery storage system. It said the projects will be connected to Saudi Arabia's 380-kilovolt (kV) transmission network and will be designed for remote operation. Al Muwayh and Haden BESS projects are located in Makkah region while Al Kahafa is located in Hail region. The three projects represent 75 percent of the 2GW/8GWh G1 programme, which has an estimated value of around $1.16 billion, according to information provided by the company. Last month, SPPC had signed 15-year Storage Service Agreements (SSAs) for the three Independent Storage Provider (ISP) projects with a consortium comprising Saudi Energy Company, ACWA Power and Al Sharif Contracting and Development Company. The SSA for the fourth project, Al Khushaybi in Qassim region, was signed with a consortium comprising ENGIE and Haji Abdullah Ali Reza & Partners Co. Ltd (HAACO). Gotion said its Gotion Grid has a 25-year design life, compared with what the company described as an industry average of 15-20 years. The system also incorporates an AI-based battery management system for dispatch, safety monitoring and lifecycle diagnostics, according to the company. Gotion said its battery storage project portfolio across the Middle East and North Africa region stands at around 9GWh. These include a 1.5GWh BESS project in Egypt, alongside plans for 3GWh of local manufacturing capacity, and a 1.2GWh project in Morocco with ACWA Power. artigo.texto: Remuneração das baterias por múltiplos serviços é o Santo Graal do mercado Foi, justamente, um modelo bem-sucedido de remuneração que levou os Estados americanos do Texas e da Califórnia a expandirem o armazenamento de energia em baterias Atualizado Depois de um crescimento acelerado nos últimos três anos, a capacidade instalada de armazenamento de energia em baterias nos Estados Unidos deverá atingir o patamar recorde de 106 GW até o fim de 2028, de acordo com projeções divulgadas pela Administração de Informação de Energia (EIA) norte-americana. Nos próximos dois anos e meio serão acrescidos 54 GW aos atuais 52 GW de capacidade de armazenamento em baterias. É um mercado dominado por fabricantes de tecnologia de ponta, integradores de sistemas e gigantes industriais, que investem pesado. A Tesla, por exemplo, está finalizando a construção de sua megafábrica de baterias em Sparks, Nevada, com capacidade inicial de 10 GW, com investimentos de US$ 3,6 bilhões. Outra gigante do setor, a LG Energy Solution está expandindo sua rede de produção de baterias para sistemas de armazenamento de energia no Michigan e no Arizona. “As políticas de precificação de energia têm criado condições favoráveis para o armazenamento de energia em baterias em alguns Estados norte-americanos, casos da Califórnia e do Texas — e isso é um diferencial muito grande em relação ao mercado brasileiro”, destaca Rafael Ferreira, presidente do conselho consultivo da Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae). Camila Ramos, diretora-executiva da Clean Energy Latin America (Cela), concorda: “O aprendizado mais valioso que a experiência norte-americana pode trazer para o Brasil não está no tamanho, na capacidade do sistema, mas no desenho de mercado”. Ela diz que na Califórnia o armazenamento em grande escala surgiu como resposta às altas abruptas de demanda e quedas rápidas da geração de energia ao longo do dia. Já no Texas, a bateria é remunerada por múltiplos serviços ao mesmo tempo. Ou seja, a bateria é remunerada por tudo o que oferece: flexibilidade, segurança e resposta rápida. “Quando o Brasil destravar a remuneração de serviços ancilares e permitir que a bateria monetize seus vários usos ao mesmo tempo, o mercado brasileiro deixará de crescer por necessidade e passará a crescer por retorno”, diz Ramos.

artigo.texto: The clean energy transition is accelerating, but choosing the right vehicle for your capital is difficult. Should you favor Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE +1.30%) or the hydrogen giant Plug Power (PLUG +2.69%)? PLUG & EOSE: Performance Comparison Key Financial Metrics Eos focuses on zinc-based batteries designed for long-duration storage, offering an alternative to traditional lithium-ion tech. Plug Power provides a comprehensive green hydrogen ecosystem, serving massive logistics fleets with fuel cells. Both companies occupy critical niches in the evolving energy landscape, making them frequent candidates for comparison among growth-oriented investors. The case for Eos Energy Enterprises Eos Energy Enterprises designs and manufactures zinc-based long-duration energy storage systems. These systems target utility-scale and industrial applications, providing a non-flammable alternative to lithium-ion batteries. In its latest annual report, filed for 2025, the company highlighted its focus on the U.S. market. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as two specific clients accounted for nearly 52% and 19% of total revenue. In FY 2025, revenue reached about $114.2 million, representing a significant increase of approximately 630% over the previous year. This rapid top-line growth shows the company is scaling its production capabilities to meet demand for industrial stocks. Despite this growth, Eos reported a net loss of nearly $970 million. This loss reflects the high costs of expanding manufacturing and the early-stage nature of its commercial rollout. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is negative 1.0x, which means total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The so-called current ratio stands at approximately 4.9x, measuring a company's ability to pay short-term debts with its current assets. artigo.texto: KIRKSVILLE, Mo. — Residents got a closer look at proposed data center regulations proposed to Kirksville's Planning and Zoning Commission this month, though no data centers have tried to move to town yet. City planner Diane Albrecht has spent the last two months extensively collecting information with the hopes of helping the city get ahead of the curve when it comes to data centers. ““If there is no permitted use, and no regulation, and if a data center were to come in, without any zoning addressing that, then it's what they call by-right development,” Albrecht explained to KTVO.” By-right development means any incoming companies would essentially be free to make their own rules as long as they’re following the existing city codes, which does not currently include data center regulations. Albrecht also says that a moratorium or outright refusal to cooperate with data centers wouldn't be a lasting or legally safe solution. “There is the real possibility of a developer suing the city or taking it to court to have that thrown out,” Albrecht said. “There are at least two cases that I know of in Missouri, Springfield and Benton County.” The regulations being proposed would confine data centers to a 4-acre, M-2 Industrial Zone within the city and ban local tax incentives. The limited space is expected to prevent any hyper-scale data centers from being built. Also included in the lengthy proposal were a hefty list of definitions, required reports, site design standards, and violation penalties. Each section of the proposed code is designed to serve as layered coverage from any potentially concerning data center impacts. Where one section of code may not cover, another is designed to. “I literally wrote down concerns that I was being given, and then we literally went through—I went through and made sure that every one of those was addressed in the best way that we could,” Albrecht assured. The proposed regulations are also expected to remain an open conversation, with improvements implemented as they’re needed and the city continues learning more about data centers. The final proposal is set to be considered by city council during a study session on October 19th, though official action isn't expected until their regular meeting on Oct. 26.
