artigo.texto: India’s carbon market is being built under pressure from a trade system in which emissions are becoming a direct cost of exporting. The European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, which entered its definitive phase in January 2026, requires importers to account for the carbon embedded in selected goods. For Indian steel, aluminium, cement and fertiliser producers, the issue is no longer only how much they manufacture or sell, but how much carbon is associated with every unit reaching a foreign market. That shift changes the meaning of industrial competitiveness. An Indian factory can comply with conventional export requirements and still face a commercial disadvantage if its production is more carbon-intensive than that of competitors. The EU importer pays the border charge, but the cost can travel back through lower margins, higher prices or reduced demand for Indian goods. The United Kingdom is preparing a similar mechanism for January 2027, widening the number of markets in which carbon intensity could influence export economics. India’s response is centred on the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, or CCTS, and on efforts to make domestic carbon pricing part of a broader industrial transition. The policy objective is twofold: retain some carbon-related economic value within India and reduce the emissions that generate charges abroad. The second objective is harder. A domestic market can allocate a price to emissions, but it cannot by itself provide the clean electricity, transmission, storage and production technologies required to lower emissions at scale. The size of the exposure makes this more than a climate-policy question. India’s merchandise exports reached $441.78 billion in FY26, according to the supplied report, while metals remained a major export category. The European mechanism currently covers iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen. These sectors are closely tied to heavy industry, energy consumption and the infrastructure of industrial production. NITI Aayog’s Trade Watch Quarterly, as cited in the report, puts India’s annual metals exports at about $34.8 billion in 2025. Iron, steel and aluminium accounted for roughly 78% of that trade. The EU represented approximately 22% of India’s combined steel and aluminium exports, while the EU exposure for iron and steel stood at 39.3%. That means the European market is not a marginal destination for Indian metal producers. For steel exporters in particular, changes in the cost of carbon can affect a substantial part of their external market. The export numbers also show why the timing matters. India exported 6.94 lakh tonnes of finished steel worth ₹5,541.2 crore in August 2026, according to the report, with volume up 31.3% and value up 41.5% from August 2025. Between April and August, finished-steel exports reached 29.86 lakh tonnes worth ₹23,646.6 crore, representing increases of 34.1% in volume and 32% in value. Strong export growth can increase exposure to carbon-related trade costs if production systems remain emissions-intensive. The structural difficulty lies in how Indian metals are produced. NITI Aayog’s Trade Watch Quarterly for April-June, or Q1 FY27, said Indian metals have notably higher carbon intensity than the global average. The report attributed this largely to the continued importance of coal-based Blast Furnace–Basic Oxygen Furnace routes in primary steelmaking and coal-fired Direct Reduced Iron processes, rather than cleaner gas-based or Electric Arc Furnace routes. This production profile means the carbon problem cannot be solved through documentation alone. Indian exporters need to measure and verify embedded emissions, but lower paperwork does not equal lower emissions. The trade system may reward accurate reporting in the short term, yet the lasting competitive advantage will come from changing the energy and technology used in factories. A June 2026 working paper by the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations estimated that India’s steel exports to the EU could fall by 24% under CBAM. The estimate is based on simulations using the ICRIER Samriddhi Model, a GTAP-E-based general-equilibrium model. It is therefore a modelled scenario rather than an observed fall in exports, but it illustrates the scale of the risk facing a sector with significant European exposure. India has begun building the administrative architecture needed to respond. The Central government notified the CCTS in June 2023 under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act. The scheme is overseen by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and uses emissions-intensity targets rather than an absolute production cap. Targets become stricter each year and operate in two-year compliance cycles beginning in FY 2025-26. According to a Press Information Bureau release cited in the report, the system covers more than 700 industrial units across seven emissions-intensive sectors, including steel, aluminium and refining. Companies that perform better than their assigned targets can earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates, with each certificate representing one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent reduction. Companies that fail to meet their targets can face penalties. The framework has also expanded to include sectors such as petroleum refining, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium. The design reflects an attempt to connect industrial performance with market incentives. Yet the value of that incentive will depend on the strength of the market and the price attached to each reduction. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative, said the EU carbon price was about €75 per tonne of carbon dioxide, compared with roughly $10 in China, while India’s emissions-trading system would take time to become fully operational. His assessment was that recognition of India’s system overseas would not necessarily remove the border charge because a substantial price gap could remain.

artigo.texto: No Brasil, um maço de cigarros carrega 83% de tributos. Um casaco de pele, 81%. Já as baterias que armazenam energia limpa e garantem a confiabilidade do sistema elétrico pagam 84%. Tributamos como supérfluo, ou como vício, um equipamento que se tornou infraestrutura essencial no mundo inteiro e que, no Brasil, poderia ajudar a reduzir a conta de luz. A distorção ganha urgência às vésperas das eleições. Com eventos climáticos extremos e mais frequentes, decisões sobre o setor elétrico dizem respeito à segurança energética e à competitividade da indústria nacional. O Brasil reúne condições únicas para liderar essa transformação: um dos melhores recursos solares do mundo e uma matriz elétrica predominantemente renovável. A energia solar já é a segunda maior fonte da matriz, fruto de uma década que mobilizou mais de R$ 320 bilhões em investimentos. Mas o sistema não foi projetado para essa velocidade. Cortes de geração renovável, inversões de fluxo nas redes e pressões tarifárias mostram que desperdiçamos energia limpa e barata enquanto o consumidor paga uma conta de luz que sobe acima da inflação. É exatamente esse o problema que as baterias ajudam a resolver. Elas armazenam energia nos momentos de maior geração e a devolvem quando o sistema mais precisa, aumentando a confiabilidade, reduzindo desperdícios e custos sistêmicos e diminuindo a dependência de combustíveis fósseis nos horários de pico. Segundo a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), o armazenamento pode atrair mais de R$ 200 bilhões em investimentos na próxima década. O que trava esse potencial é, em boa medida, a tributação. Corrigi-la não é conceder subsídio: é dar às baterias tratamento isonômico em relação às demais tecnologias do setor elétrico. Enquanto essa distorção persistir, a sociedade seguirá exposta a riscos operacionais e custos desnecessários. O próximo governo também precisará evitar retrocessos. A inclusão recorrente de “jabutis” em projetos de lei para privilegiar combustíveis fósseis aumenta a conta dos consumidores e indica ao mercado uma direção na contramão do mundo. Cada política pública deve ser guiada pela eficiência e pelo interesse coletivo. A transição energética precisa ser política de Estado, com planejamento, estabilidade regulatória e visão de longo prazo. Aos candidatos deste ano, fica uma pergunta: por que o Brasil ainda cobra mais imposto da bateria do que do cigarro? Quem tiver a melhor resposta estará mais preparado para decidir o futuro energético do País.

artigo.texto: Lao Cai se prepara para participar do mercado de créditos de carbono florestal. Na tarde de 29 de setembro, o Sr. Phan Trung Bá, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial, presidiu uma reunião para discutir o desenvolvimento de serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono, a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa e a exploração eficaz do potencial e das vantagens florestais, preparando assim as condições necessárias para que Lao Cai participe do mercado de créditos de carbono florestal. Estiveram presentes na reunião líderes dos Departamentos de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, Finanças, Indústria e Comércio, Construção, Ciência e Tecnologia; do Subdepartamento de Proteção Florestal e do Fundo Provincial de Proteção Florestal e Ambiental. Segundo um relatório do Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, na implementação do Decreto Governamental nº 180/2026/ND-CP sobre serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono florestal, a província de Lao Cai está gradualmente concluindo seu banco de dados e preparando as condições necessárias para o desenvolvimento de projetos de carbono florestal. Até o momento, a província concluiu o levantamento do estado das florestas e das reservas de carbono florestal em 48 municípios e distritos da região norte. Os resultados indicam uma reserva total de carbono de 14,33 milhões de toneladas. O Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente finalizou o esboço e o orçamento para o levantamento do estado das florestas para o período de 2026-2027 em 51 comunas e distritos da região sul, servindo como base para a construção de linhas de referência para projetos de carbono na província. Além de investigar e avaliar o potencial, a província está preparando as condições necessárias em termos de mecanismos, projetos e recursos para desenvolver créditos de carbono florestal. O Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente prestou consultoria sobre o desenvolvimento de conteúdo relacionado à gestão e ao uso de créditos de carbono; elaborou o documento do projeto "Transformando os Resultados da Redução de Emissões e a Gestão Florestal Sustentável no Vietnã, Província de Lao Cai", financiado pelo Fundo Verde para o Clima (GCF). Simultaneamente, está desenvolvendo o plano técnico e o orçamento para o projeto de créditos de carbono em florestas de propriedade de toda a população. Você também pode gostar Segundo o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, os projetos de desenvolvimento de carbono florestal são uma área nova, sendo implementados pela primeira vez na província. O processo de implementação ainda requer aprimoramento em diversas áreas, principalmente no que diz respeito aos requisitos técnicos, padrões econômico -técnicos, sistemas de medição, relatórios, avaliação e verificação dos resultados da redução de emissões. Na reunião, os delegados concentraram-se na discussão da investigação e desenvolvimento de uma base de dados florestal e de carbono; métodos de medição, monitorização e digitalização de dados; recursos para implementação; e as condições necessárias para a implementação do projeto de crédito de carbono florestal na província. Ao concluir a reunião, o Sr. Phan Trung Bá, Vice-Presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial, enfatizou que o desenvolvimento de créditos de carbono florestal está passando da fase de pesquisa para a implementação concreta, com demandas cada vez maiores em relação a dados, base legal, recursos e capacidade de implementação. Portanto, o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente precisa assessorar proativamente e preparar dados de entrada suficientes sobre florestas, como base para a integração com o sistema geral de dados e para servir à gestão e ao desenvolvimento do mercado de carbono. O camarada solicitou ao Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente que continue investigando e atualizando o estado atual das florestas em 51 comunas e distritos; e, ao mesmo tempo, revise e delimite especificamente as áreas florestais, especialmente naquelas onde a entidade gestora não foi claramente identificada. Com isso, o objetivo é completar gradualmente o banco de dados florestal e preparar as condições para o desenvolvimento de créditos de carbono na província. Você também pode gostar Em relação aos recursos para implementação, o camarada Phan Trung Bá solicitou ao Departamento de Finanças que revisasse e assessorasse sobre a alocação de verbas para atividades de proteção florestal, levantamentos do estado das florestas e implementação de projetos de carbono florestal. Quanto ao orçamento proposto, ele enfatizou que se trata apenas de uma estimativa inicial, servindo de base para o desenvolvimento de um plano e orçamento detalhados. O uso dos recursos deve ser calculado com base em normas estabelecidas, conteúdo e etapas reais de implementação, garantindo a conformidade com as normas e a eficácia. O vice-presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial também enfatizou que a gestão e a exploração de informações e dados sobre carbono florestal devem ser realizadas com rigor. Organizações e empresas que necessitem realizar levantamentos e avaliações de recursos florestais para projetos de carbono devem ser orientadas de acordo com as normas, prevenindo o risco de exploração indevida de levantamentos e avaliações para fins de exploração, troca ou transferência de informações e dados sobre recursos de carbono. Além disso, o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente, em coordenação com o Departamento de Ciência e Tecnologia, está pesquisando soluções tecnológicas e equipamentos para apoiar a investigação, medição e coleta de dados sobre florestas; e preparando informações para integrar e digitalizar gradualmente os dados florestais da província. O vice-presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial, Phan Trung Bá, solicitou que os departamentos e agências continuem a coordenar pesquisas e a fornecer consultoria sobre a avaliação da capacidade de absorção de carbono das florestas; proponham soluções para melhorar a qualidade e o valor das flor

artigo.texto: Czech Republic and Italy Propose Easing the European Carbon Market Prague and Rome present a joint package to the European Council aimed at adjusting the carbon market, free allocations and methane obligations to reduce industrial energy costs. Andrej BabiÅ¡, the Czech prime minister, and Giorgia Meloni, president of the Italian Council of Ministers, presented a joint package of proposals intended for the European Council meeting of October 15 and 16, 2026, in Brussels. The document, titled "Energy costs and European industrial competitiveness," was published on September 30, 2026, by the Office of the Czech Government, a day after a bilateral meeting at the Strakova akademie in Prague. It aims to ease the energy costs borne by European industry through adjustments to the carbon market and to fossil fuel supply rules. An alternative to a general suspension of the carbon market According to Prague and Rome, a general suspension of the European emissions trading market would not have sufficient support among member states. The package therefore proposes targeted adjustments to the Market Stability Reserve, the mechanism that regulates the supply of allowances auctioned according to predefined rules. The two governments are requesting the ability to reduce or suspend withdrawals from this reserve and, if necessary, to organize an exceptional release of allowances. The volume concerned would correspond to a flow withdrawn from auctions, distinct from the reserve's total stock. Free allocations and the role of electricity The text also calls for greater flexibility in the allocation of free emission allowances, which protect certain industrial activities against the risk of production relocating to jurisdictions with weaker carbon constraints. Both countries are seeking a revision of the performance benchmarks used to calculate these allocations, as well as a pause in their reduction for sectors already covered by the carbon border adjustment mechanism. For electricity, the package envisions a temporary adjustment of the carbon obligations imposed on fossil-fuel plants that set the market's marginal price. Prague and Rome are also requesting greater recognition of the transitional role of gas and of nuclear power within the European taxonomy of sustainable investments. Certain nuclear and gas-related activities are already included, under conditions, as investments considered sustainable. The package does not specify the additional criteria that would be applied to broaden this recognition. Methane obligations and a new carbon market for buildings On methane, the initiative seeks the temporary suspension of obligations relating to fossil fuel imports. Current European regulation requires importers to demonstrate the equivalence of the monitoring, reporting and verification measures applied to the production of crude oil, natural gas and coal, with a different treatment for pre-existing contracts. The package finally calls for a reassessment of the launch of the new emissions trading system covering buildings, road transport and other sectors, separate from the existing carbon market and whose obligations fall on fuel suppliers. The two governments propose a postponement conditional on its effects on the energy crisis, along with coordinated monitoring of financial positions in this market, without establishing the existence of any manipulation. The publication of this package confirms the two governments' common position, without constituting an adoption of the measures by the European Union.

artigo.texto: No dia 29 de setembro, a Academia Vietnamita de Ciências Florestais, por meio do Centro Vietnamita de Certificação de Gestão Florestal (VFCC), em colaboração com a Forest Trends, organizou um workshop de consulta sobre "Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN) para a Restauração Florestal Após a Extração Mineral e Oportunidades de Participação no Futuro Mercado de Carbono". Restauração florestal após mineração: abrindo oportunidades para participar do mercado de carbono. (Chinhphu.vn) - De acordo com especialistas, a aplicação de soluções NbS não só ajuda a regenerar a vegetação nativa e a restaurar ecossistemas danificados pela mineração, como também abre grandes oportunidades para que empresas e localidades participem do mercado de carbono no futuro. Durante o workshop, especialistas argumentaram que, embora muitas commodities que representam risco de desmatamento, como madeira, café, borracha, soja e óleo de palma, estejam sujeitas a requisitos de controle cada vez mais rigorosos, as atividades de mineração, apesar de seu impacto significativo nas florestas, ainda não foram inseridas em uma estrutura de governança proporcional. O Dr. To Xuan Phuc, especialista da Forest Trends, observou que o impacto da mineração na vegetação e nos ecossistemas florestais está se tornando cada vez mais evidente, mas os minerais raramente são reconhecidos como uma "mercadoria com risco de desmatamento". Isso cria uma lacuna nas políticas públicas, já que a cadeia de suprimentos de minerais ainda não atende aos requisitos equivalentes em relação à responsabilidade pela proteção e restauração florestal. Essa ausência cria uma lacuna significativa em termos legais e políticos. Enquanto os produtos de madeira e café passam por rigorosos processos de due diligence para verificar sua origem não desmatada antes de entrarem em mercados exigentes, a cadeia de suprimentos de minerais carece de obrigações comparáveis em relação à proteção e restauração florestal. Segundo especialistas, as atividades de mineração podem levar à perda de vegetação, perturbar a estrutura do solo, fragmentar habitats, aumentar o risco de deslizamentos de terra e poluir fontes de água. Análises de sensoriamento remoto também mostram um declínio na cobertura vegetal em muitas áreas de mineração, enquanto a infraestrutura que serve à mineração pode aumentar a pressão sobre as florestas próximas. No Vietnã, foram emitidas regulamentações sobre a conversão de terras florestais e os depósitos para restauração ambiental, mas sua implementação ainda é limitada. A restauração pós-florestamento em algumas áreas não restaurou completamente as funções ecológicas da floresta e não está intimamente ligada aos padrões de manejo florestal sustentável. Integrar a restauração florestal na governança da mineração. Dr. Tran Lam Dong , Vice-Diretor da Academia Vietnamita de Ciências Florestais. Conclusão: É hora de as agências reguladoras mudarem sua mentalidade e considerarem o controle do impacto da indústria de mineração nas florestas como parte integrante da estratégia nacional de proteção florestal e resposta às mudanças climáticas. Especialistas propõem considerar os minerais como um fator de controle de risco para o desmatamento, estabelecer padrões obrigatórios de responsabilização e avaliações de impacto florestal para projetos de licenciamento de mineração; fortalecer os mecanismos de coordenação intersetorial e conectar estreitamente as agências de gestão de recursos minerais e as agências de gestão florestal ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida do projeto de mineração, desde o planejamento e licenciamento até o fechamento da mina e a restauração ambiental. Uma das abordagens discutidas no workshop foi a aplicação de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN) para restaurar áreas florestais impactadas pela mineração. O professor Vu Tan Phuong, diretor do Centro de Certificação de Gestão Florestal do Vietnã (VFCC), afirmou que a aplicação de soluções de NbS não só ajuda a regenerar a vegetação nativa e a restaurar ecossistemas danificados pela mineração, como também abre grandes oportunidades para que empresas e localidades participem do mercado de carbono no futuro. Segundo o Professor Vu Tan Phuong, as áreas onde as operações de mineração são restauradas, se devidamente reflorestadas e restauradas ecologicamente de acordo com os padrões de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN), gerarão um sequestro significativo de carbono. Esse aumento nos estoques de carbono pode ser medido, relatado e verificado (MRV) para ser convertido em créditos de carbono florestal de alta qualidade. Isso oferece um benefício duplo: apoia as empresas no cumprimento de suas responsabilidades sociais e ambientais, ao mesmo tempo que gera financiamento adicional com a venda de créditos de carbono nos mercados nacional e internacional, criando um incentivo econômico intrínseco para o reflorestamento pós-mineração. artigo.texto: One of the first power purchase agreements for space-based solar is being announced today, and it’s with a data center. Virtus Solis Technologies, a Michigan-based startup working to put solar panels into space, signed a 20-year PPA with startup Brae Systems, which hopes to use the electricity — beamed back to Earth from satellites — to power the data centers it plans to build, not on land but underwater. Per the agreement, Virtus Solis will provide 100 megawatts of 24/7 orbital solar power, amounting to over 875,000 megawatt-hours annually; Brae has the option to increase the agreement to 250 MW within three years from initial commercial operations. Unlike a PPA for a typical solar project, power delivery is still years away — if it comes at all. John Bucknell, Virtus Solis founder and CEO, told Latitude Media he expects first power to happen around 2030, roughly when Brae Systems plans to launch its first megawatt-scale underwater data center. A lot needs to happen, including actually proving out the technology, in the interim. “There are technical and financial milestones associated with both sides,” Bucknell said. “We agree to deliver power in the future… and they agree to purchase [it]. But obviously, we need to do our fiduciary duty along the way, and so do they.” For Virtus Solis, the milestones include putting a 100-kilowatt pilot plant into orbit within the next 24 months and securing project financing for its first 100 MW power plant, among other things. But — as was true when Commonwealth Fusion Systems signed its first PPA with Dominion Energy in late 2024 — a PPA for a technology that hasn’t yet been proven at commercial scale is a symbolic as much as a financial agreement. In this case, it demonstrates that the market’s interest in space-based solar is becoming very real, as data centers’ need for power extends to encouraging even the most nascent technologies. Momentum has also come by way of Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which earlier this year filed with the FCC for permission to deploy an orbital data center “constellation.” The SpaceX concept, however, would have both the energy source and the compute located in space, with data sent back to Earth via optical links. Virtus Solis, meanwhile, takes a more “traditional” approach to space-based solar, Bucknell said. It aims to put solar cells in orbit, “where the sun always shines,” convert the energy into radio waves, and beam it back to Earth, where antennas would then receive them and convert them back into electricity once again. “We operate in radio frequency physics as opposed to photovoltaic physics,” Bucknell said. “The power plants just happen to have an element in orbit and an element on the ground.” The advantage of this approach is that solar power can be harvested at its maximum intensity 24/7, unencumbered by the cycle of night and day or by weather. It’s an idea that has existed for several decades, albeit in a niche corner of the energy and tech worlds, but has always been too expensive to become a reality. In fact, what is believed to be the first PPA for space-based solar was actually signed in 2009 between PG&E and startup Solaren, for 200 MW of capacity to be delivered starting in 2016. The contract was mutually cancelled in 2015, after Solaren failed to secure financing for its technology. Bucknell says the prices of solar cells, electronics, and commercial space launches have since collapsed, making the idea more viable today than it was a decade ago. Next steps For the Brae Systems PPA, Virtus Solis’ plan is to launch its satellites on commercial heavy-lift rockets, such as the ones SpaceX operates, and assemble them in orbit into arrays of up to two kilometers across. Once in orbit, the arrays will beam radio waves down to a receiver station in Illinois, where the data center developer — clearly not shy about technological experimentation — plans to submerge its first data centers in the cooling ponds of a retiring coal-fired power plant. The radio waves would then be converted back into electricity and used to power the data center behind the meter. The plan’s success hinges on many factors. So far, Virtus Solis has not announced any funding raises and has operated mostly in stealth “for the last number of years,” Bucknell said, financing its operations through a mix of venture capital and government funding. The latter includes a roughly $2-million ARPA-E award won in January 2025 to develop the power electronics needed to make its wireless power transfer more efficient. The company plans to show the results of the work it has done for this award in a public demonstration scheduled for March 2027. Bucknell hopes that the demo will show that more than 50% of the electricity sent through its wireless link comes out as usable electricity on the other end; previous demos only managed about 4%. But for this project, it would have to also find project financing, which can be tricky for the most cutting-edge technologies — though a PPA certainly helps. And while it’s true the price of rocket launches has decreased since 2009, it’s certainly not cheap to get things into orbit. A commercial launch with SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket costs $74 million. “All by ourselves, just this first power plant would be hundreds of launches of the Falcon series, and I think 18 launches of the Starship series,” Bucknell said. The prices of commercial launches with SpaceX’s Starship rockets, the most advanced model that has so far only done text flights, aren’t public at the moment. Plus, while submerged data centers exist, most notably in China, they’re not in wide use yet, and Brae has yet to announce a successful deployment. Ultimately, the company aims to deploy its data centers in the deep sea, “where it’s nice and cold,” to replace the need for expensive cooling systems, according to Bucknell. But that would require using undersea cables to connect to Virtus Solis’ ground power plant, which come with a high price of their own. None

artigo.texto: The Clackamas County Board of County Commissioners will hold two public hearings to consider adopting a temporary moratorium on data center development in unincorporated Clackamas County. The hearings give community members a chance to share their opinions on the potential moratorium and provide concerns and other feedback about data centers. Public hearing dates: Wednesday, Oct. 21, 6 p.m. Board Meeting Room, 4th floor Clackamas County Public Services Building 2051 Kaen Road Oregon City, OR Thursday, Oct. 22, 10 a.m. Board Meeting Room, 4th floor Clackamas County Public Services Building 2051 Kaen Road Oregon City, OR Can't attend in person or virtually? You can submit written testimony to bcc@clackamas.us, and it will be included in the record. What to expect County staff will provide information about the criteria for establishing a moratorium. The staff presentation will focus on those criteria. Staff will not propose changes to county code related to data centers during these hearings. If the Board adopts a moratorium, public input received during the hearings could help inform the Board's consideration of future code changes. About data centers Data centers are facilities that house computer systems and related equipment used to store, process, and manage digital information. The growth of artificial intelligence and cloud computing is contributing to increased data center development nationwide. Data centers can involve considerations related to land use, energy, water, infrastructure, noise, and other factors. The National Association of Counties (NACo) has developed an informational resource for county officials that provides an overview of data center development and topics counties may consider as they evaluate local regulations. Learn more: NACo Informational Primer and County Considerations: Data Centers

artigo.texto: A WEG anunciou a ampliação do projeto da nova fábrica de sistemas BESS, de armazenamento de energia em baterias, em construção em Itajaí. Anunciada em fevereiro deste ano, a unidade terá investimento estimado de R$ 330 milhões e capacidade anual de 4 GWh. A nova fábrica vai atender à demanda ligada à transição energética e tem início das operações previsto pro segundo semestre de 2027. O projeto reforça a estratégia da empresa de acompanhar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, que está prestes a lançar o primeiro leilão de baterias, previsto ... O projeto reforça a estratégia da empresa de acompanhar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, que está prestes a lançar o primeiro leilão de baterias, previsto pra dezembro. Na atualização do projeto, a WEG incorporou maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial que permitirão ampliar a capacidade produtiva. Continua depois da publicidade A fábrica contará com linhas automáticas e semiautomáticas de montagem, além de robôs móveis autônomos para movimentações internas. O complexo também terá um laboratório de testes, desenvolvimento e qualificação de produtos, responsável por aprimorar processos, garantir o controle de qualidade e acelerar a criação de novas soluções em baterias. Segundo o vice-presidente de automação e sistemas da WEG, Manfred Peter Johann, o investimento está alinhado à forte expansão do mercado de armazenamento de energia, impulsionado pelo crescimento das fontes renováveis e pela necessidade de maior flexibilidade e segurança pro sistema elétrico. “A ampliação deste projeto demonstra a capacidade da WEG de adaptar rapidamente seus investimentos para atender às necessidades do mercado e apoiar o desenvolvimento sustentável do setor energético brasileiro”, comenta. As baterias produzidas em Itajaí vão ajudar na estabilidade do sistema elétrico, na eficiência operacional e no aproveitamento dos recursos energéticos. O BESS, sigla em inglês para Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias, é uma tecnologia avançada que armazena energia elétrica em grandes baterias. A solução tem papel importante nos sistemas elétricos modernos, principalmente na integração de fontes renováveis, como solar e eólica, permitindo guardar energia nos momentos de maior disponibilidade e ofertá-la quando necessário.

artigo.texto: Kern supervisors approve new solar, battery storage near California City BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) – The Kern County Board of Supervisors have approved a new solar project for the county. The Board approved the request to build a solar facility called the Galaxy Solar PV and Storage Project, which developers say will bring millions of dollars to the county. With the Board's new approval, Terra-Gen, the solar development company, can take the next step forward in constructing the solar facility, which will generate 600 megawatts of electricity and four gigawatt-hours of battery energy storage. Craig Murphy, director of the Kern County Planning & Natural Resources Department, told the Board of Supervisors on Tuesday, Sept. 29, that the project is proposed to be built on 184 parcels – about 3,519 acres – of land in California City. He said the project would be built and live on the southern side of Highway 58, approximately 2,900 feet east of Highway 14, straddling both the north and south sides of Silver Queen Road. County documents show that project's site is on privately owned land in unincorporated areas of southeastern Kern County. Sam Sours, Terra-Gen's vice president of solar development, told the Board on Tuesday afternoon that the Galaxy Solar project is estimating about $16.1 million in property taxes during its first full year of operation. He said the project is expected to generate about $120 million in property tax contributions over the facility's 35-year lifespan. Sours added that the project would help the state meet its goal of 60% of electric retail sales by 2030. He said the project will employ about 350 people – 650 workers during peak times of construction – and that the facility's employees will be hired through a local union labor, adding that the worker's agreement has already been signed. With the project's approval representatives from Terra-Gen said that Joshua Trees in the vicinity of the project will be moved wholly and rerooted in a tree sanctuary in Los Angeles County. artigo.texto: Battery energy storage is rapidly becoming an essential part of the energy transition. Yet, while technology itself has developed significantly, the financing of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects is still evolving, particularly in markets where storage is relatively new. In my experience, one of the main challenges is not necessarily the maturity of the technology itself, but the level of understanding of what a BESS project really involves from a financing perspective. As the European BESS market scales, the next challenge is increasingly important: enabling these assets to access bank financing and project finance structures. A bank is not simply financing a battery. It is financing an asset expected to generate revenues and perform reliably for many years. Therefore, bankability needs to be considered much earlier than financial close. Bankability should start at the design stage One of my strongest recommendations to developers is to start discussing financing requirements with lenders while the project is still being designed. Too often, financing is considered after the technology has been selected and the main supply contracts are already substantially negotiated. By then, changing certain contractual or technical conditions can be difficult and expensive. The project should begin with a robust financial model and a clear understanding of the expected return on investment and revenue structure. At this stage, developers should already be engaging not only with potential lenders, but also with financial and technical advisers and key technology partners. Understanding what lenders will require can influence technology selection, contractual structures, guarantees, operating strategy and even project design. In other words, bankability should be designed into the project rather than tested at the end of it. Revenue certainty remains fundamental A technically excellent BESS project without a credible revenue model will remain difficult to finance. This is one of the major differences between storage markets today. There is already considerable experience in more mature European storage markets, particularly in Great Britain, Poland, Belgium and Italy, where capacity mechanisms or dedicated storage procurement schemes provide BESS projects with access to contracted revenue streams. Italy's MACSE, for example, represents a particularly interesting development as a mechanism specifically designed to procure electricity storage capacity. Other markets, including Spain, are now developing their own capacity mechanisms and moving towards a framework in which storage can increasingly access long-term contracted revenues. Where this type of framework is not available, developers need to build credible alternatives. Depending on the market, these may include tolling or swap agreements (including revenue-floor structures), PPAs or other offtake arrangements designed to reduce merchant exposure and provide greater revenue certainty. Batteries have the advantage of being able to access multiple revenue streams, but flexibility should not be confused with certainty. From a lender's perspective, the question is not simply how many markets a battery can participate in, but how predictable those revenues are throughout the financing period. There is also an important connection between revenue and technology: the operating profile assumed by the financial model must remain compatible with the technical capabilities and warranty conditions of the BESS. The bankability of the supplier matters too Technology selection is obviously important, but lenders look beyond technical specifications. They need confidence in the company standing behind the technology. Supplier financial strength, manufacturing capability, track record, supply-chain resilience and the ability to provide long-term technical support all become part of the risk assessment. The same applies to the complete system architecture. Batteries, PCS, EMS and other critical components need to comply with applicable technical requirements, certifications and grid codes. Traceability of materials and components, quality control, manufacturing procedures and regulatory project documentation are increasingly relevant parts of technical due diligence. For an asset expected to operate for 15 or 20 years, the question is therefore not simply whether the technology performs today. The lender also needs confidence that the supplier and service structure can support that performance over time. Ultimately, bankability becomes contractual This is perhaps one of the areas that is sometimes underestimated. When lenders and their advisers analyse a BESS project, many technical and financial assumptions eventually need to be translated into contractual protections. Payment milestones, Advance Payment Bonds, Performance Bonds, Warranty Bonds, letters of credit and their corresponding wording can all be subject to review. The lender will want to understand what protects the investment from the first payment through delivery, commissioning and long-term operation. This extends to delivery obligations, transfer of title and risk, delay liquidated damages, performance liquidated damages, acceptance procedures, commissioning requirements, warranties, liability limits and available remedies. The objective is not to eliminate every project risk; that would be impossible, but to understand who carries each risk and what happens if the underlying assumptions are not achieved. Performance guarantees must match the financial model Degradation is a good example of where technical, commercial and financial assumptions meet. A financial model may assume a certain available capacity or energy throughput over 10, 15 or 20 years. The lender therefore needs confidence that these assumptions are technically realistic and appropriately supported. Performance warranties should consequently be assessed alongside expected cycling, depth of discharge, C-rate, temperature

artigo.texto: Schneider Electric Unveils World's First Software-Defined Medium Voltage Switchgear to Expand AI-Ready Data Center Power Portfolio - World's first fully Software-Defined Medium Voltage architecture enables up to 3× faster ordering and manufacturing, up to 2× faster commissioning and zero-downtime upgrades - RM AirSeT™ 38 Software Defined extends Schneider Electric's SF₆-free medium-voltage technology to 38 kV for high-density, scalable data center architectures "The challenge facing data center operators today is not just keeping pace with AI growth, but building the resilient, efficient and scalable power infrastructure needed for an increasingly digital world," said Frédéric Godemel, Executive Vice President, Software-Defined Medium Voltage establishes a new category of power infrastructure Building on its broader Software-Defined Energy vision, Based on the comparison documented in Schneider Electric White Paper 303, the approach enables up to 3× faster ordering and manufacturing, up to 2× faster commissioning and onsite acceptance testing, compared with conventional engineered-to-order medium-voltage switchgear. It also reduces system complexity: in the 20-panel comparison, the software-defined configuration used 87% less control wiring, 91% fewer terminals and 85% less copper in that wiring, while providing digital connectivity and analytics for greater operational visibility. Key elements of the Software-Defined MV architecture include: - Standardized, configurable infrastructure: Replaces highly customized, engineered-to-order systems with modular hardware that can be standardized and deployed more quickly. - Software-enabled functionality: Shifts capabilities from hardware into software, allowing customers to add new features and performance improvements without physical modifications. - Digital-first deployment: Standardized modules, automated testing, and intuitive interfaces help streamline ordering, manufacturing, commissioning, and onsite acceptance. - Lifecycle flexibility: Over-the-air updates enable system upgrades without hardware replacement or operational downtime, while software-enabled capabilities support ongoing optimization and AI-powered predictive maintenance through EcoCare Services. The Software-Defined MV approach has been deployed in live operation through a pilot with Equinix in a colocation data center environment. Pilot programs continue through 2027, with broader availability to follow in 2028. To learn more, visit the Software-Defined MV switchgear page or read the Software-Defined MV white paper. To receive product and availability updates, register your interest. RM AirSeT 38 meets that need, giving hyperscalers and colocation providers greater flexibility as they modernize their electrical distribution strategies. RM AirSeT 38 is designed to support high-density, scalable deployments through: - SF ₆ -free technology: Uses pressurized pure air insulation and vacuum interruption technology instead of SF₆ (sulfur hexafluoride, a potent greenhouse gas), fluorinated gases, or proprietary gas mixtures. - Compact GIS design: Supports space-constrained, high-density installations while enabling standardized, repeatable MV architecture across data center deployments. - Software-defined capabilities: A standardized digital architecture designed to simplify configuration, accelerate commissioning and support lifecycle evolution. - Operational visibility: Digital monitoring and sensing options provide visibility into system performance, configurable to each customer's cybersecurity requirements. Order intake is planned to begin in 2027, with first deliveries expected in 2028. To receive updates on RM AirSeT 38, register your interest. Key benefits include: - Industry-leading power density: Delivers up to 1.25 MW in a single frame while using up to 70% less space than predecessor systems, helping customers maximize IT capacity and floor space. - Optimized efficiency and sustainability: Galaxy VXL is designed to drive energy-efficient operations, lowering total cost of ownership, and support long-term sustainability initiatives – delivering a 31% reduction in lifecycle CO₂ emissions compared with its predecessor. - Validated for AI workloads: Designed for the dynamic power profiles associated with AI clusters and high-density compute environments, helping ensure power quality, resilience, and availability. - Scalable, service-friendly architecture: Schneider Electric's third-party verified Live Swap technology lets operators add, upgrade, or replace power modules without planned downtime, supporting future expansion while maintaining uptime. - Digital-first operations: Integrated EcoStruxure™ monitoring and digital services provide visibility, predictive maintenance, and lifecycle optimization across critical power infrastructure. Availability Galaxy VXL is available globally and supports both Lithium-ion and VRLA battery technologies, providing customers with flexible energy storage options to meet their resiliency, performance, and sustainability requirements. artigo.texto: Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and China's Gotion have agreed plans for three battery joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco, involving combined estimated investment of approximately €3.22bn ($3.65bn). Gotion is expected to invest about €1.59bn, while PowerCo – Volkswagen's battery manufacturing subsidiary – will contribute approximately €1.62bn. The ventures are planned to produce lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells and cathode materials in Valencia, Šurany and Kenitra. Volkswagen Group technology management board member and PowerCo supervisory board chairman Thomas Schmall said: "This marks a major breakthrough for both companies and brings us one step closer to the forefront of electric mobility. "Volkswagen is the first European automotive manufacturer to cover the entire battery value chain, from development and cathode materials through to production." In Valencia, PowerCo's under-construction gigafactory is expected to transfer into a joint venture producing LFP cells, with an annual capacity of 29.1GWh. PowerCo will hold 51% and Gotion 49%, making the venture a controlled PowerCo subsidiary. Gotion is expected to invest about €1.1bn for its stake. The Valencia facility is intended to serve as a European production hub for Volkswagen's LFP-based Unified Cells. Gotion's planned cell factory in Šurany will also transfer into a joint venture. The facility will have an annual capacity of 8.4GWh and produce LFP cells for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Gotion will own 51%, with PowerCo holding 49%. In Kenitra, the companies plan to establish a facility producing 100,000t of LFP cathode material annually. Gotion will retain a 51% stake, while PowerCo will own 49%. The project is intended to diversify supply sources for key cathode active materials. PowerCo is expected to contribute approximately €470m to the Šurany and Kenitra projects by 2030 for its 49% stake in each project. The agreement extends a partnership that began in 2020 and covers joint procurement and sales activities in Europe. The transactions remain subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, including approval from Gotion shareholders and governmental approvals in China and overseas. Gotion said implementation would take place in phases. Volkswagen Group, through its subsidiary Volkswagen (China) Investment, has also entered definitive agreements to sell a 5.3% equity stake in Gotion. The company said its voting rights, board representation, nomination rights and position as a strategic investor would remain unchanged after completion.

artigo.texto: Companies sign MOU to explore collaboration on deployable structures, spacecraft integration and scalable architectures for in-orbit Artificial Intelligence and edge computing LAS VEGAS , Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sophia Space and Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW), a global leader in aerospace and defense technology solutions, today announced they have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to advance the development and deployment of scalable computing infrastructure in orbit, combining Sophia Space's modular orbital compute architecture with Redwire's extensive technology solutions in deployable space systems, solar power generation and distribution, heat management and rejection, spacecraft integration, avionics, and systems engineering. Under the MOU, the companies will explore collaboration across near-term demonstration missions and longer-term orbital data center architectures. Sophia Space is developing a new class of computing infrastructure designed specifically for the space environment. Its modular TILE architecture integrates high-performance computing, solar power and passive radiative thermal management into scalable systems designed for Artificial Intelligence (AI) inference, data processing and other compute-intensive workloads in orbit. By combining Sophia Space's compute architecture with Redwire's space infrastructure and engineering capabilities, the companies aim to address one of the central challenges facing the emerging orbital computing market: moving from individual technology demonstrations toward the repeatable, scalable infrastructure needed for the global build-out of orbital data centers. "We're past the point of asking whether high-performance computing belongs in orbit," said Rob DeMillo, CEO and Cofounder of Sophia Space. "The question now is how quickly we can scale it. Redwire brings the deployment and systems expertise that can help us move from individual missions to persistent computing infrastructure in orbit. That is the transition we're building toward now." "The demand for global computing is scaling exponentially, and the advancement of orbital data centers represents an exciting paradigm shift where space infrastructure can scale critical capacity beyond the constraints of terrestrial infrastructure," said Al Tadros, Chief Technology Officer, Redwire Space. "As a leading space infrastructure provider, Redwire is translating the maturation of the orbital data center market into exciting opportunities to build next-generation architectures that could unlock significant economic value. Sophia Space and Redwire intend to jointly pursue select U.S. government and commercial opportunities, including potential programs involving DARPA, the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL), the Space Development Agency (SDA) and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). Areas of potential collaboration include concept development, joint proposals, internal research and development activities, customer engagement, and international market opportunities. --- About Sophia Space Inc. Sophia Space is building the future of orbital computing and in-space data centers. Its modular TILE technology enables passive computing alongside in-situ data processing, AI acceleration, and edge computing for satellites, defense systems, and commercial space stations, dramatically reducing latency and delivering actionable insights where and when they are needed. Learn more at www.sophia.space About Redwire Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW) is an integrated space and defense tech company focused on advanced technologies. We are building the future of aerospace infrastructure, autonomous systems, and multi-domain operations leveraging digital engineering and AI automation. Redwire's approximately 1,400 employees located throughout North America and Europe are committed to delivering innovative space and airborne platforms transforming the future of multi-domain operations. For more information, please visit RDW.com. Media Contacts: David Ariosto, Executive Director, Communications, Sophia Space [email protected] Tere Riley, Vice President Marketing Communications, Redwire [email protected] View original content to download multimedia:https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sophia-space-and-redwire-team-up-to-advance-orbital-data-center-infrastructure-302893808.html SOURCE Sophia Space

artigo.texto: Volkswagen battery unit PowerCo and Chinese battery maker Gotion have announced joint plans to invest around €3.22bn (US$3.68bn) in three battery and materials joint ventures across Spain, Slovakia and Morocco. Gotion’s board approved the proposal the same day, though the companies have yet to sign a formal investment agreement, and the deal still requires shareholder approval and government clearances in both China and Europe. The largest project in Valencia, Spain, calls for a €2.26bn investment to build 29.1 GWh of annual lithium-ion battery capacity. Gotion will acquire a 49% stake in the existing PowerCo Spain entity through a capital increase, with PowerCo retaining 51% control. That structure follows local media reporting in July that the two companies were in advanced talks over a Gotion stake in the Valencia plant specifically. Visits were made by Gotion Chief Executive Li Zhen to evaluate the site, and PowerCo said at the time it had no plan to cede control. With a 51% stake, this remains the case—albeit only just. A second project in Šurany, Slovakia, involves a €480m investment for 8.4 GWh of annual capacity and will see this ownership structure put in reverse: Gotion takes 51% and PowerCo 49%. A third joint venture, also split 51-49 in Gotion’s favour, will invest €480m in a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials plant in Kenitra, Morocco. The companies expect 100,000 metric tons of annual capacity from the plant, which will supply the two European battery projects. Cells from the Spanish and Slovakian plants will prioritise Volkswagen’s own European demand, though specific purchase volumes remain subject to separate definitive agreements. The expansion deepens an already substantial equity relationship: Volkswagen’s Chinese investment arm held a 24.28% stake in Gotion as of 20 September, making it the battery maker’s largest shareholder. While small compared to giants CATL and BYD, Gotion’s global electric vehicle battery installations reached 34.0 GWh over the first seven months of 2026, up 44.2% year-on-year. The company ranked fifth globally with its market share rising from 3.9% to 4.7%, according to SNE Research. The Gotion partnership is one piece of a substantially larger battery strategy Volkswagen has been building since founding PowerCo in 2022. At the core of this strategy is a standardised prismatic ‘Unified Cell’ architecture, designed to power more than 80% of future vehicles across the Group’s sprawling brand portfolio. The battery’s external cell dimensions stay identical regardless of application, but the internal chemistry varies depending on the segment’s needs. Low-cost LFP and eventual sodium-ion are intended for the entry-level offerings, while high-nickel, nickel-manganese-cobalt and eventual solid-state technology are reserved for the premium end. PowerCo operates its own gigafactories on a ‘Standard Factory’ blueprint, using identical building layouts, machinery and IT systems across sites specifically to speed deployment and reduce capital expenditure, with plants in Valencia; Salzgitter, Germany; and St. Thomas, Ontario together targeting up to 200 GWh of annual capacity. Upstream, the unit’s Ionway joint venture with Umicore, is building a cathode and precursor materials facility in Nysa, Poland aimed at supplying enough material for roughly 2.2 million electric vehicles a year by 2030. PowerCo has a stated goal of reducing battery pack costs to less than US$100 per kWh. This will depend on running a standardised architecture across every partner simultaneously: Gotion for LFP engineering and Asian volume, QuantumScape for solid-state licensing, CATL and LG Energy Solution for current MEB-platform demand. Thus, the Gotion joint ventures function less as standalone deals than as one component of a supply network in which the automaker is deliberately remaining technology-agnostic and geographically diversified. Reversing the ownership split between the Spanish project, where PowerCo retains control, and the Slovak and Moroccan projects, where Gotion holds the majority stake, suggests Volkswagen is calibrating how much operational control it cedes to its Chinese partner by asset type. It is keeping its most strategically important European cell plant under direct control while relying on Gotion’s expertise for smaller, more specialised capacity.

artigo.texto: The companies behind the proposed Marshall Springs battery energy storage system (BESS) and solar project agreed to largely halt site development last Thursday, Sept. 24, after agreeing to the terms of a temporary injunction filed against them by Gillespie County. Marshall Springs Storage, LLC; Marshall Springs Solar, LLC; and AMPYR Energy USA, LLC agreed to the injunction as a compromise to avoid a contested hearing. The agreement does not constitute an admission by the companies or waive either side’s claims or defenses in the case. The agreement comes after AMPYR’s lawyers attempted to get the county’s temporary injunction order thrown out by the state district court earlier this summer. In August, the court ruled against AMPYR’s dismissal bid. Now that the two sides have agreed, a hearing over the temporary injunction that was set for Tuesday, Sept. 29, has been canceled. The county’s lawsuit over the BESS and solar farm project is scheduled for trial in June 2027. Per the terms of the temporary injunction, the defendants have agreed to pause the following actions until the conclusion of the trial: - tree or brush clearing - grading, digging or drilling - stockpiling materials or equipment such as panels, batteries and containers - building roads, pads, structures or utility lines - altering creeks or drainage - installing wells or septic systems - bringing crews or equipment onto the site to prepare for any of that The companies are still permitted to perform certain tasks on the property. They may construct and maintain a single access road from Texas Highway 16 to the property, use the site for agricultural purposes, including grazing, haying and maintaining livestock water, perform routine maintenance and survey the property. The agreed order also states that the property lies wholly or partly within an area of special flood hazard regulated by the county’s Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance. The order says a development permit is required before development occurs in that area and that no such permit has been issued for the property. The parties have also been ordered to mediate. They must agree on a mediator by Oct. 9 and conduct mediation by Oct. 31. The two sides will meet for trial in the 216th Judicial District Court of Gillespie County at 9 a.m. June 7, 2027. Background Back in March, the county filed a lawsuit against three companies that are behind a BESS site and solar project that is proposed on more than 1,100 acres near Texas 16 North and Clear Springs Road, north of Fredericksburg. Marshall Springs Storage, LLC; Marshall Springs Solar, LLC; and AMPYR Energy USA, LLC are listed as the defendants in the case. The county has argued that a large-scale lithium-ion battery storage facility poses a significant threat to the safety of local residents because of its potential for fire and environmental damage. According to the National Fire Protection Association, lithium-ion batteries can catch fire or explode if damaged, improperly charged or improperly stored. The Fredericksburg Fire Department has said it cannot properly respond to a fire caused by a lithium-ion battery malfunction. The county also argues the project’s location is inappropriate because it sits in an area devastated by the 2025 Crabapple Fire, which burned nearly 10,000 acres. It contends a battery fire could quickly grow out of control and threaten nearby watersheds through pollution.

artigo.texto: Parcerias Crusoe Revela Papel de Desenvolvedor no Campus de Data Center de IA da Google no Texas Adicione Unite.AI às suas fontes preferidas no Google Crusoe anunciou em 28 de setembro de 2026 que é a desenvolvedora do campus de data center da Google em construção no Condado de Armstrong, nos arredores de Amarillo, Texas, um projeto que a empresa disse ser projetado para fornecer capacidade para alimentar IA avançada e onde mais de 5.500 trabalhadores qualificados estão no local diariamente. “Construir o futuro da IA requer um novo tipo de infraestrutura, começando pela energia. A estratégia da Crusoe é construir fábricas de IA diretamente na fonte de energia abundante e de baixo custo – tanto para melhorar a utilização dos ativos existentes quanto para catalisar a geração de nova energia”, disse Chase Lochmiller, CEO e cofundador da Crusoe, em o anúncio da empresa. Lochmiller descreveu o campus do Condado de Armstrong como um exemplo dessa estratégia centrada na energia e afirmou que a empresa está colocando energia limpa, nova e acessível em operação no local. A construção começou em junho de 2025 e continua em andamento, de acordo com o anúncio, que afirmou que o projeto está trazendo investimento significativo e empregos para a comunidade local. Lochmiller disse que a Crusoe está construindo no mesmo ritmo acelerado que estabeleceu em Abilene. Conexão Direta ao Vento e Projeto de Resfriamento O campus tem uma conexão direta com o parque eólico Goodnight 1 adjacente a Serena, uma instalação de 265,5 MW que está operacional, e o parque eólico Goodnight 2, também de 265,5 MW, que está em construção e foi catalisado pelo desenvolvimento da Crusoe no local. Quando a geração eólica excede a demanda do campus, o excedente de energia é devolvido à rede, um arranjo que Crusoe disse beneficiar os consumidores locais e reduzir a limitação da energia eólica do oeste do Texas. O projeto utilizará um sistema de resfriamento líquido de circuito fechado e não evaporativo que a Crusoe afirmou ser projetado para limitar significativamente a pegada hídrica da instalação, destinando-a principalmente a usos domésticos, como cozinhas. O Modelo de Energia Across the Meter Em uma postagem no blog publicada no mesmo dia, a Crusoe descreveu o modelo “across the meter” por trás do design do campus: co‑locar data centers de IA na fonte de geração para capturar energia que de outra forma seria limitada ou abandonada. A postagem afirmou que as áreas mais ventosas e as mais adequadas para produção solar costumam estar em locais remotos com demanda local limitada, o que pode levar os preços da energia a valores negativos quando a geração excede o consumo local, uma dinâmica agravada pela congestão de transmissão, já que muitas usinas enviam energia pelas mesmas linhas para mercados urbanos distantes. O post da Crusoe cita o Independent Market Monitor para o Relatório Estado do Mercado 2025 da ERCOT, que constatou que aproximadamente 4,7% da geração eólica foi reduzida em 2025, e uma estimativa da U.S. Energy Information Administration de que aproximadamente 5% da eletricidade é perdida durante a transmissão e distribuição. A empresa afirmou que seu modelo de negócios original levou data centers modulares a locais remotos de produção de petróleo para capturar gás que, de outra forma, seria queimado, e que a mesma lógica agora se aplica à energia renovável encalhada. Sob o design across-the-meter, um campus extrai energia incremental da rede quando a geração local é insuficiente e envia energia excedente para a rede quando a geração local supera a carga do campus. A Crusoe disse que a carga co‑locada também oferece aos desenvolvedores de renováveis um incentivo orientado pelo mercado para repotenciar e atualizar turbinas envelhecidas, porque os sites eólicos e solares existentes já possuem terras permitidas, acordos de interconexão e relacionamentos comunitários. Investimento na Comunidade e Portfólio do Oeste do Texas O anúncio informou que o investimento local na comunidade também inclui o Texas Energy Impact Fund da Google, que recentemente anunciou apoio a melhorias de eficiência em edifícios públicos e residências no Condado de Armstrong. A Google divulgou os primeiros beneficiários do fundo em 21 de maio de 2026, como parte de um compromisso de US$ 30 milhões com a resiliência e a acessibilidade energética no Texas. A postagem da Google informou que os beneficiários inaugurais incluem a Energy Management Alliance, financiada para expandir o treinamento de gestores de energia para comunidades rurais e financiar melhorias de eficiência em edifícios públicos nos Condados de Armstrong, Ellis, Haskell e Wilbarger, juntamente com reparos residenciais pré‑climatização nesses quatro condados por meio da Solar United Neighbors, do Texas Energy Poverty Research Institute e da aliança, e na região de Houston por meio do Houston Advanced Research Center. As bolsas do Texas Energy Poverty Research Institute financiam desafios de inovação focados em resiliência, acessibilidade e eficiência energética para edifícios multifamiliares e cooperativas elétricas, enquanto a Solar United Neighbors implantará energia solar, baterias e bombas de calor em residências de baixa renda e como centros de resiliência comunitária no Condado de Ellis, segundo a postagem. A Crusoe afirmou que seu portfólio em expansão no oeste do Texas reforça ainda mais a região como crítica para o futuro da infraestrutura digital americana. Juntamente com o campus do Condado de Armstrong, o portfólio inclui dois campuses em desenvolvimento em Abilene.

artigo.texto: German carmaker Volkswagen and Chinese battery manufacturer Gotion plan to invest some €1.5 billion ($1.7 billion) to expand their partnership, the companies said on Monday. Volkswagen and Gotion aim to set up three joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco to "accelerate the development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe." Under the plans, which are dependent on regulatory approval, a gigafactory currently being built by Volkswagen's battery division PowerCo in Valencia is to be transferred into a joint venture, alongside Gotion's plant in Surany, Slovakia. Volkswagen and Gotion also aim to set up a new production facility in Kenitra, Morocco, "to produce cathode material for LFP batteries." All three ventures are to be managed jointly, the companies said. Volkswagen subsidiary PowerCo is to invest some €470 million by 2030 to acquire a 49% stake each in the Slovakian and Moroccan sites. In return, Gotion is to spend some €1.1 billion to acquire a 49% stake in the Valencia factory. Volkswagen's battery division PowerCo, which was established in 2022, is responsible for the development and production of battery cells. Its first factory in Germany's Salzgitter began production at the end of 2025, with another plant under construction in St. Thomas, Canada.

artigo.texto: Meta (NASDAQ:META) cut its taxes by $3.9 billion in 2025 with research tax credits, up from $2 billion in 2024 and $700 million in 2023, according to the company's securities filings. A New York Times investigation published Sept. 30 reported that Meta classifies its AI data centers as "pilot models" for tax purposes — the term federal tax rules use for test versions of a product built to resolve open questions during development. The Times cited four people familiar with Meta's operations. Meta uses that label to claim a federal research tax credit on the Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips inside the data centers, a practice the Times dates to late 2024. Meta did not immediately respond to Moneywise's request for comment. A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change Meta's second-quarter guidance calls for $130 billion to $145 billion in spending this year on buildings and equipment, much of it to build out AI computing power. "AI is accelerating our core business today," CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in the same release. No other publicly traded company gets more out of the credit, according to a Times review of securities filings. How Meta's research tax credit strategy reportedly works The credit dates to 1981, when lawmakers worried Japan was pulling ahead in technology, according to the Times. Most companies claim it mainly on what they pay researchers and engineers. Supplies can count too. IRS guidance says they have to be used in "qualified research," meaning experiments to solve a technical unknown. Meta treats its chips as supplies in that kind of research, according to the Times. The IRS has pushed back before when companies tried to claim the credit on off-the-shelf equipment, the Times reported. Andre Shevchuck, who leads the research tax credit practice at California-based advisory firm BPM, told the Times the approach is "kind of wild and out there." "Meta is claiming billions of dollars in tax benefits that its own accountants are telling investors are at risk of being overturned by the IRS," Lisa De Simone, who teaches accounting at the University of Texas and previously worked as a tax adviser at EY, told the Times. Former Rep. James Shannon, D-Massachusetts, sponsored the credit in 1981. He told the Times it was meant to support "people power, knowledge, information." When he heard a tech company was claiming it for AI data centers, Shannon said, "This has gone way, way beyond what anybody could have imagined." Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said the company has put $200 billion into research and development over the past five years, $57 billion of it last year. "Like other companies that invest at this scale, we use the tax incentives Congress established decades ago to encourage this type of domestic investment," Stone said in a statement to the Times. How much the research tax credit costs taxpayers Congress' Joint Committee on Taxation projects the research credit will cost the government $32.1 billion in corporate tax revenue in fiscal year 2025. By the Times' math, Meta's share tops 10%. JCT expects that cost to climb every year, to $41.3 billion by fiscal 2029. Over five years, the total comes to $183.2 billion — more than any other corporate tax break except a lower tax rate on U.S. companies' overseas profits. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) claimed $1.05 billion in research credits for its 2025 fiscal year. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) claimed about $2.09 billion in federal research credits in 2025. Meta's $3.9 billion beats the two combined. It's also 15 times the $260 million in research tax credits that Merck (NYSE:MRK) claimed in 2025. Merck makes the cancer drug Keytruda. Shevchuck told the Times the approach might work "if you had a data center that you're building out to cure cancer." EY — Meta's auditor and one of the firms that advised it on the credit — has taken the chip strategy to other companies, according to the Times. Meta is separately set to receive $3.3 billion in state and local tax breaks for its Hyperion data center in Louisiana. Meta's IRS fights and $18.74B in uncertain tax benefits Meta and the IRS are also in U.S. Tax Court over an earlier research credit claim. The agency wants back about $355 million in credits that Meta tied to $4.1 billion in Zuckerberg's stock compensation from 2012 and 2013, according to Bloomberg Tax. Meta argues Zuckerberg personally wrote code and oversaw Facebook's technology in 2005, when it granted the options. The IRS points to the option contract, which says the options weren't payment for anything Zuckerberg did before 2008. In a separate case over how Meta priced deals with its own foreign subsidiaries, the IRS says the company shifted profits to the Cayman Islands. The agency is seeking nearly $16 billion, including penalties, according to the Times. Meta is fighting the case in Tax Court, its annual filing shows. Meta's gross unrecognized tax benefits — tax savings it has claimed but hasn't counted toward its profits because they might not hold up — reached $18.74 billion as of June 30. That's up 45% from $12.91 billion two years earlier. Meta says those benefits are primarily tied to "uncertainties with our research tax credits" and its foreign-subsidiary deals. Meta's June 2024 filing listed the foreign-subsidiary issue first. Three months later, research credits had moved to the top. Stone called the figure "a snapshot in time." What Meta's tax fight means for shareholders If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you own a piece of Meta. Meta has been warning shareholders of the risk, and those $18.74 billion in benefits are excluded from the profits it reports. If its positions hold up, Meta says $12.73 billion of that would flow back into earnings. Often, even when the IRS objects, massive companies like Meta can negotiate settlements that let them keep part of the savings and come out ahead to the delight of shareholders. artigo.texto: BSES holds industry workshop on BESS safety As battery energy storage becomes an increasingly important part of India’s clean-energy transition, BSES recently organised a three-day workshop on the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Safety Framework, bringing together power-sector leaders, global safety experts, utilities, fire and emergency services and industry professionals. The workshop focused on a priority: ensuring battery storage scales up safely, responsibly, and with the right level of preparedness. Discussions covered safety-by-design, early warning and detection, thermal runaway, recognised testing, emergency preparedness, evacuation protocols and first-responder readiness. The inaugural session was addressed by Ghanshyam Prasad (Chairperson, CEA); Amal Sinha (Director & Group CEO, BSES); Abhishek Ranjan (CEO, BRPL); Sunil Kumar Jha (Director General, FS, CD & HG); Santosh Kumar (COO, BYPL); Alok Kumar (Director General, AIDA); Asko Rajput (Chairman, Standards Committee, BIS); Tanya Singhal (Vice President & Country Head, GEAPP); and Dr Rashi Gupta (MD, Vision Mechatronics Pvt Ltd). The workshop moved beyond discussions to practical preparedness. A major highlight was a live thermal runaway demonstration in a battery module, followed by firefighting intervention by Delhi Fire Service personnel. The exercise helped participants understand how battery failures can develop and the challenges emergency responders may face. Global experts Richie Stephen (Senior Standards Project Manager, UL Standards & Engagement), Kurt Vollmacher (Director, Intotech & Fire Safety Trainer) and Dr Judy Jeevarajan (UL Standards & Engagement) shared insights on system testing, failure modes, manufacturing defects, battery ageing, fire safety and emergency response, drawing on experience. The workshop concluded with nine multidisciplinary teams working through emergency scenarios involving smoke at a BESS site, flooding at an installation, and post-fire dismantling and waste management. The exercise helped participants identify priorities, responsibilities and the safest course of action. The programme also drew on BSES’ experience with its pioneering 20 MW/40 MWh Kilokri BESS, reinforcing the need to keep safety at the heart of storage growth.
