artigo.texto: Crusoe Developing Data Center Campus in Armstrong County, Texas Data center to be built at the source of West Texas clean energy CLAUDE, TX – September 28, 2026 – Crusoe, the AI factory company, today announced it is the developer of Google’s data center campus under construction in Armstrong County outside of Amarillo. The campus is engineered to provide capacity to power advanced AI. “Building the future of AI requires a new kind of infrastructure, starting with energy. Crusoe’s strategy is to build AI factories directly at the source of abundant, low-cost energy – to both improve utilization of existing assets as well as catalyze new energy generation,” said Chase Lochmiller, CEO and Co-founder of Crusoe. “The Armstrong County campus is a prime example of this energy-first strategy. We're bringing new, affordable clean energy online. We broke ground in June 2025 and are building at the same swift pace we set in Abilene.” The campus has a direct connection to Serena's adjacent Goodnight 1 (265.5 MW) wind farm, which is operational, and Goodnight 2 (265.5 MW) wind farm, which is currently under construction and was catalyzed by Crusoe’s development at the site. When wind generation exceeds campus demand, surplus power is supplied back to the grid – benefiting local ratepayers and reducing curtailment of West Texas wind energy. By co-locating directly at the source of West Texas wind energy, Crusoe’s approach actively supports the region's buildout of clean, affordable energy. In addition to its innovative energy sources, the campus is designed for water efficiency. The project will utilize a closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system, which is designed to significantly limit the facility's water footprint to primarily domestic uses such as kitchens. Construction broke ground in June 2025 and is underway, with more than 5,500 skilled laborers on-site daily, bringing significant investment and employment to the local community. Local investment in the community also includes Google’s Energy Impact Fund, which recently announced support for efficiency upgrades in public buildings and homes in Armstrong County. The campus is part of Crusoe's growing West Texas portfolio, which includes two campuses under development in Abilene, further establishing West Texas as a critical region for the future of American digital infrastructure. Read more about Crusoe's energy approach here: www.crusoe.ai/resources/blog/co-located-power-for-ai-data-centers. About Crusoe As the AI factory company, Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. The company provides a reliable, scalable, cost-effective, energy-first solution for AI infrastructure. By harnessing large-scale energy sources, building AI-optimized data centers, and delivering a powerful AI cloud platform, Crusoe empowers its customers and partners to build the future faster. For more information, visit crusoe.ai. Media Contact: media@crusoe.ai

artigo.texto: Redata encontra fila de mais de 56 GW por energia para data centers EPE tenta separar projetos reais dos que podem não sair do papel; expansão já exige R$ 1,6 bilhão em novas obras de transmissão só em São Paulo A sanção do Redata colocou combustível em uma corrida por data centers que começa a esbarrar em um recurso mais difícil de encontrar do que terrenos: energia disponível para conectar os novos empreendimentos. O presidente da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), Thiago Prado, afirmou neste mês que já existem mais de 56 gigawatts (GW) em pedidos de acesso à rede feitos por projetos de data centers. O próprio executivo fez uma ressalva importante: uma parcela dessas iniciativas provavelmente não sairá do papel, e a estatal está procurando investidores para entender o grau de maturidade dos projetos antes de recomendar novas expansões da infraestrutura elétrica. A cifra mostra a velocidade com que o mapa mudou. Pouco mais de 60 dias depois da primeira versão do Redata, editada em setembro de 2025, a EPE havia registrado um salto de 19,8 GW para 26,2 GW apenas entre os projetos que protocolaram no Ministério de Minas e Energia pedidos de estudo para conexão à Rede Básica. Ou seja: naquele curto intervalo, surgiram 6,4 GW adicionais de demanda potencial. Agora transformado em lei, o Redata foi sancionado em 15 de setembro. O regime reduz a carga tributária sobre a compra e a importação de equipamentos de tecnologia utilizados nos centros de dados, incluindo a suspensão de PIS/Cofins, IPI e, em determinadas condições, Imposto de Importação. O objetivo é diminuir um dos custos que tornavam o Brasil menos competitivo para instalações voltadas a computação em nuvem, processamento de alto desempenho e inteligência artificial. O incentivo tributário, porém, resolve apenas uma parte da equação. A corrida pela tomada Grandes data centers são consumidores de eletricidade de escala industrial. E a velocidade de construção dessas instalações não necessariamente acompanha a expansão do sistema elétrico. Prado estima que uma grande unidade possa ser erguida em cerca de três anos, enquanto uma nova linha de transmissão pode levar aproximadamente cinco anos. É esse descompasso que começa a preocupar o planejamento do setor. São Paulo, que concentra a maior parcela do mercado brasileiro, dá a dimensão do problema. A EPE já recomendou aproximadamente R$ 1,6 bilhão em novos investimentos de transmissão no estado para liberar cerca de 4 GW de margem para novas conexões. Outros estudos podem acrescentar mais 5 GW de capacidade. E a pressão não está restrita ao estado. A estatal prepara estudos para viabilizar da ordem de 4 GW de novos projetos no Rio de Janeiro; analisa no Rio Grande do Sul empreendimento com demanda que pode chegar a 5 GW; e trabalha em soluções capazes de aumentar em outros 4 GW a capacidade de conexão de grandes cargas no Nordeste. Os números de pedidos de energia são muito maiores do que o mercado efetivamente em construção — justamente uma razão para a cautela da EPE. Levantamento da consultoria imobiliária JLL aponta atualmente 660 MW de data centers em construção no país, capazes de atrair cerca de US$ 17,4 bilhões em investimentos, além de outros 4.621 MW no pipeline. A taxa de vacância nacional está em apenas 4%, e 56% do estoque novo em construção já havia sido pré-locado. Energia limpa também entra na conta O próprio desenho do Redata transforma a disponibilidade de energia em peça central da escolha de onde construir. Para usufruir do regime, o data center terá de atender 100% de sua demanda elétrica com contratos de suprimento ou autoprodução provenientes de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão. A lei também estabelece limite de eficiência hídrica e obriga investimentos em pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação. Parte dos detalhes ainda é remetida a regulamentação. Há ainda uma exigência de que pelo menos 10% da capacidade beneficiada seja destinada ao mercado brasileiro — obrigação que pode ser substituída, nos termos previstos pela lei e sua regulamentação, por investimentos adicionais em pesquisa e desenvolvimento O resultado é uma mudança na lógica da disputa imobiliária que acompanha o boom dos data centers. Não basta mais ter uma grande área disponível. O endereço valioso é aquele que combina terreno, fibra óptica e, principalmente, megawatts que possam efetivamente chegar ao empreendimento. Com o Redata reduzindo a barreira tributária para os equipamentos, é justamente essa disputa pela tomada que tende a definir quais dos dezenas de gigawatts hoje apresentados ao sistema elétrico virarão data centers de verdade.

artigo.texto: NineDot Energy opened a large battery storage site in the Bronx, New York. Company leaders joined elected officials and community groups to cut the ribbon on a project replacing a former fuel oil trucking facility. By the time next summer’s heat waves arrive, this setup will be fully ready. It will deliver almost 20 megawatts of power to the community, enough energy to power about 20,000 homes during the busiest times for the grid. Addressing the Environmental Issues For decades, Hunts Point residents have dealt with serious environmental issues. For example, local leaders say that more than 10,000 diesel trucks pass through the area daily. Additionally, two high-emissions “peaker” power plants operate nearby. These plants only run when the grid needs extra power, but they produce heavy pollution. Advertisement This new site stores energy and releases it during peak hours. This means older gas-fired plants won’t have to run as much, and eventually, they can be retired. It also provides reliable energy as the local produce market, fish market, and truck fleets switch to electric power. “We’re honored to bring this battery storage site to the Hunts Point community,” said Adam Cohen, NineDot’s Chief Technology Officer and Co-founder. “Hunts Point has historically been overburdened by high-emitting fossil fuels, and this battery storage facility marks an inflection point in improving the local environment and grid reliability.” Storing Energy for Years to Come During the extreme heat wave from July 1 to 4, 2026, NineDot’s community batteries helped ease the strain on the electric grid. Across nine projects, they sent nearly 34 megawatts of power to Con Edison’s system when it was needed most. That is like taking 50,000 window air conditioners off the grid, or powering 34,000 homes for four hours a day. NineDot currently has 11 operating projects across Staten Island and the Bronx, making it the largest battery fleet in Con Edison’s city territory. The company plans to hit 400 megawatts of battery storage by the end of 2026, with over 60 more projects already in the works.

artigo.texto: PARIS LA DÉFENSE--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 1, 2026-- Regulatory News: Arkema (Paris:AKE) continues to invest in the battery business value chain and announces a €10 million expansion project for its Global Battery Center of Excellence located in Oullins-Pierre-Bénite, in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of France. This investment reflects the Group's strategy of continuously strengthening its research capabilities in advanced materials for batteries within its global network of R&D laboratories covering the entire battery value chain. Following the inauguration in Normandy in September 2025 of a laboratory dedicated to solvent-free battery electrode manufacturing, as well as several investments in Asia and the Americas, this expansion further strengthens a particularly dense global R&D network, that combines the expertise developed in France with that of the Group’s research centers in China, South Korea, Japan and the United States. Thanks to this international organization, Arkema is accelerating the development of innovative solutions capable of addressing the technological and industrial challenges of next-generation batteries. Located at the heart of the Rhône-Alpes Research Center, the Battery Center of Excellence is entering a new phase of its development. Its footprint will be tripled, and its research infrastructure will be modernized, including notably a significant increase in the digitalization of R&D activities. This expansion will consolidate the role of this French center as Arkema’s global reference platform for the development of advanced materials serving both current batteries and the next generations under development. The project will enable the Group’s R&D teams to prepare for the future industrial standards of cell manufacturers and accelerate the integration of Arkema’s advanced materials into their production processes. By replicating their customers’ manufacturing conditions, researchers will be able to better anticipate implementation constraints and contribute to the development of more efficient batteries delivering greater energy density, faster charging times and enhanced safety. “This investment marks a major milestone in Arkema’s ambition to support the rapid evolution of the battery market. By strengthening our Battery Center of Excellence in France, we are equipping our global network and teams with state-of-the-art tools that will enable them to develop, in close collaboration with our customers, the materials that will contribute to the performance of tomorrow’s batteries,” said Armand Ajdari, Arkema’s Chief technology Officer. The implementation of this project has been made possible in particular through the support provided by the French Research Tax Credit (Crédit d’Impôt Recherche) and by the French State as part of the France 2030 program. Building on its unique set of expertise in materials science, Arkema offers a portfolio of first-class technologies to address ever-growing demand for new and more sustainable materials. With the ambition to become a world leader in Specialty Materials, the Group is structured into three complementary, resilient and highly innovative segments dedicated to Specialty Materials - Adhesive Solutions, Advanced Materials, and Coating Solutions - accounting for some 85% of Group sales in 2025, and a Primary Materials segment regrouping well-positioned large scale industrials activities. Arkema offers cutting-edge technological solutions to meet the challenges of, among other things, new energies, access to water, recycling, urbanization and mobility, and fosters a permanent dialogue with all its stakeholders. The Group reported sales of around €9.1 billion in 2025 and operates in some 55 countries with 20,700 employees worldwide. artigo.texto: VIDEO — How to Stop Data Centers in Your Backyard and Beyond Published Sep 30, 2026 Hear from experts and organizers on the ground on our winning efforts to stop Big Tech’s AI data centers from invading our communities. Fran Caracappa wasn’t expecting to join a campaign against a data center in her small New York town of East Fishkill. “How I came to this fight was by chance,” she said. She was looking at a report from the New York grid operator and found a proposal for a whopping 1GW data center facility in an area of her town near a childcare center and a house of worship. Fran and her neighbors immediately jumped into action to stop this energy-hungry, water-guzzling facility. After months of organizing with Food & Water Watch and other allies, the people of East Fishkill won an incredible victory: a three-year moratorium, or freeze, on new data centers. East Fishkill’s story is echoing in communities across the country. People are unearthing data center deals, organizing with their neighbors, and successfully standing up to Big Tech. At our September Livable Future LIVE, we sat down with Fran and Food & Water Watch experts to learn how you can take on a data center in your backyard and beyond. Watch the Full Event Below! What you’ll learn from “How to Stop Data Centers in Your Backyard and Beyond” (click to expand) Hear from Ben Murray, Food & Water Watch Senior Researcher, Eric Weltman, Food & Water Watch New York Senior Strategist and Organizer, and Fran Caracappa of East Fishkill on: - What data centers are and how they threaten our environment and economy; - How we won a data center moratorium in New York and what we need next; - Six principles to guide your fight against a data center; - What information you need about the planning process and local decision-makers to successfully stop a data center; - How to communicate about data centers to bring more neighbors into the fight; - How to find out if there’s a data center planned for your community; - The myth of data centers as “economic development”; - What closed-looped cooling is and why it won’t solve data centers’ water problems; - And more! artigo.texto: Battery energy storage: 6 security questions operators should be asking Tue, 29th Sep 2026 (Today) Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) play a critical role in grid stability and renewable energy utilisation. But as these infrastructures become more sophisticated, the risk of cyberattacks grows, potentially compromising operations, safety and energy reliability. In Centrii's recently published GRIDLOCK report, using risk modelling to analyse what an attack on BESS would cost the grid, it put the chance of a major coordinated attack on the UK's battery storage fleet at 92% within the next five years. The estimated financial cost is between £2 billion and £10 billion. But what's interesting from our analysis is that the probability of an attack falls as the security investment and enhancements increase. For example, under voluntary improvements adopted gradually and unevenly across the sector, the probability falls to 78%. With mandatory IEC 62443 certification and attack-readiness drills, it fall to just 61%. BESS are not passive assets. They are software-controlled, grid-interactive systems that directly influence frequency, load balancing and stability. The integration of IT and OT in energy storage systems increases their vulnerability. As more countries shift toward long-duration energy storage, these systems could face more frequent attacks. The issue is whether operators and asset owners are prioritising security. These are the questions every operator should be asking: 1. Do I have visibility into my distributed assets? When operators lose visibility into distributed assets, whether that's down to communication failures, misconfigurations, or malicious interference, the response becomes reactive rather than coordinated. Unlike centralised generation, battery assets are often remote and dispersed, and heavily dependent on real-time telemetry. Last year's attacks on Poland's power grid show just how threat actors understand how to manipulate remote locations simultaneously to destabilise critical power networks. Without continuous, validated visibility into operational states, operators are managing blind. 2. What happens if dispatch signals are manipulated? Battery systems do not just store energy; they respond to it. Charging and discharging decisions are driven by automated signals tied to grid frequency, market conditions, and control system inputs. If signals are altered, delayed, or spoofed, the behaviour of the battery changes accordingly. A coordinated manipulation of dispatch signals could cause batteries to discharge during peak stress or charge when supply is already constrained. At scale, this could become a major grid stability event. 3. How secure is my remote access infrastructure? Remote access is critical to today's energy operations. But it's also one of the most consistently exploited pathways into operational environments. The challenge is not just whether remote access exists, but whether it is continuously monitored, authenticated and segmented. One example of a UK battery facility revealed remote connectivity and VPN management as key vulnerabilities before security improvements were made. Without robust controls these pathways could directly access systems responsible for charging discharging and grid interaction. Remote access must be treated as a critical control point, or it becomes an attacker's shortcut. 4. Are my OT systems designed for today's threat environment? Many battery installations rely on industrial control systems (ICS) originally designed for isolated environments. But in today's environment, SCADA platforms, battery management systems and programmable logic controllers are connected to external networks. While this enables efficiency and scalability, it also exposes them. Advisories by CISA in the US have highlighted vulnerabilities in widely used ICS components, including unauthorised command execution, denial-of-service conditions, or system manipulation. In the UK BESS example, outdated firewalls, irregular patching and poor segmentation led to exploitable conditions within the operational environment. 5. Is cybersecurity being managed at the speed of deployment? The simple fact is that battery storage is being deployed faster than many operators can secure it. According to the IEA, global energy storage capacity is expected to grow more than six-fold by 2030. As growth accelerates, it creates a gap between what is operationally critical and what is operationally secured. In practice, this gap shows up in incomplete asset inventories, delayed patch cycles and limited monitoring of newly deployed systems. When basic vulnerabilities exist, attackers will always sense an opportunity. 6. Do I understand how cyber risk translates into financial impact? Cybersecurity in energy is often framed as a data protection issue. In BESS environments, it is an operational and financial issue. The GRIDLOCK report backs this up. It estimates that bringing the UK's battery storage infrastructure up to IEC 62443 Security Level 2 – the standard the modelling shows meaningfully reduces attack probability – would cost between £400m and £1bn across the national fleet. This is a return on proactive security investment of roughly 5x to 25x. The earliest likely attack window also changes, from 2027–28 under a baseline posture to 2029–31 under the most rigorous one. What's clear is that security investment reduces risk, but also buys time The grid is becoming far more distributed, connected and automated – and BESS is at the heart of this energy transformation. Distributed control without distributed visibility creates fragility rather than resilience. For operators the question is not whether cybersecurity matters, but why it matters.

artigo.texto: Mercado de carbono abre espaço para o agro regenerativo A transição, porém, exige investimentos iniciais O mercado de créditos de carbono no solo pode se tornar uma fonte adicional de financiamento para a expansão da agricultura regenerativa no Brasil. A combinação entre o potencial agrícola do país, a disponibilidade de áreas para recuperação e a busca por sistemas produtivos de baixo carbono abre espaço para remunerar produtores pela adoção de práticas que aumentem o estoque de carbono e melhorem a qualidade do solo. Análise do Rabobank aponta que o Brasil reúne condições para se tornar um dos principais mercados de créditos de carbono no solo do mundo. Dados da Embrapa citados pelo banco mostram que, dos 177 milhões de hectares de pastagens existentes no país, cerca de 28 milhões de hectares, equivalentes a 15% do total, apresentam algum nível de degradação e poderiam ser restaurados com práticas regenerativas. A transição, porém, exige investimentos iniciais, mudanças no manejo e um período de adaptação. Entre os benefícios associados à agricultura regenerativa estão o aumento da matéria orgânica do solo, ganhos de produtividade, maior retenção de água e redução dos riscos relacionados ao clima. Nesse cenário, o Rabobank avalia que será necessário ampliar os mecanismos de financiamento e remuneração ambiental. Entre as alternativas estão prêmios em cadeias de suprimento sustentáveis, linhas de crédito com condições preferenciais e pagamentos por serviços ambientais, incluindo os créditos de carbono. O mercado já conta com metodologias para medir e monitorar o aumento do carbono armazenado no solo. No Brasil, os primeiros projetos avançam pelas etapas de validação, monitoramento e emissão de créditos. Segundo a análise elaborada por Andrés Padilla, Fernanda Casagrande e Roberto Strumpf, do Rabobank, a expansão dependerá do avanço dos projetos, da adesão dos produtores, do crescimento da demanda, da segurança regulatória e da manutenção da integridade ambiental.

artigo.texto: Jacobs to deploy data center digital twin for NVIDIA’s R&D facility DALLAS – Jacobs (NYSE: J) has been selected by NVIDIA to deploy its Data Center Digital Twin for a large-scale R&D facility in the United States. Under a three-year software-as-a-service agreement, Jacobs will deploy a digital twin environment to enhance operational planning and improve facility performance across one of NVIDIA's most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) research and development facilities. Built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, Jacobs' Data Center Digital Twin creates a real-time environment that helps operators simulate scenarios, while monitoring and optimizing facility performance. The platform integrates engineering models, operational technology and live facility data into a single operational platform, giving operators greater visibility into infrastructure performance. Jacobs Executive Vice President Amer Battikhi said: “As digital infrastructure rapidly scales, operators need smarter and more connected ways to optimize performance and manage energy demand, while improving resiliency. Jacobs is integrating real-time data and simulation technologies to help NVIDIA advance the next generation of AI infrastructure management. The project reflects the growing role of digital twins in helping operators manage critical infrastructure environments.” The digital twin solution will support predictive and simulation-driven use cases including dynamic power load balancing, energy forecasting, liquid coolant leak detection monitoring, predictive maintenance and operator training. Teams can model changing AI workloads to better understand power availability and cooling performance. Beyond visualization and simulation, Jacobs is evolving the digital twin into an intelligent operating system for AI factories, where AI agents continuously learn from facility data to predict conditions, recommend actions and optimize operations with increasing autonomy. The award builds on Jacobs’ work with NVIDIA advancing digital twin technology for AI infrastructure and advanced data center environments. Jacobs is also delivering high-performance computing environments for organizations including Hut 8 in the U.S., SINES DC Campus by Start Campus in Portugal and PsiQuantum in Australia. At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow – delivering outcomes and solutions for the world’s most complex challenges. With approximately $12 billion in annual revenue and a talent force of approximately 47,000, we provide end-to-end services in advanced manufacturing, cities & places, energy, environmental, life sciences, transportation and water. From advisory and consulting, feasibility, planning, design, program and lifecycle management, we’re creating a more connected and sustainable world. See how at jacobs.com and connect with us on LinkedIn, Instagram, X and Facebook. artigo.texto: Projeto de níquel na Indonésia avança com plano híbrido de solar e armazenamento A Indonésia avançou com um projeto híbrido de energia solar fotovoltaica e armazenamento de energia em baterias desenvolvido pela PT. Kolaka Nickel Indonesia, segundo comunicado da fonte. A instalação fica em Oko Oko, Pomalaa, na Regência de Kolaka, no Sudeste de Sulawesi, e combina um parque solar de 20 MWp com um sistema de armazenamento de energia de 20 MW / 30 MWh. O projeto representa um investimento corporativo em energia limpa autogerada, destinado a apoiar operações industriais. O financiamento foi obtido em janeiro de 2026 por meio de financiamento sem recurso de três bancos: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Indonesia) Limited, também conhecido como ICBC Indonesia; Standard Chartered Bank Indonesia; e China CITIC Bank International Limited, ou CNCBI. A contratante de engenharia, aquisição e construção é a The 11th Design & Research Institute of Electronics Industry Co., Ltd., referida como EDRI. Essa empresa supervisionará o projeto, a aquisição e a construção da instalação de solar com armazenamento. Os módulos fotovoltaicos de alta eficiência da usina estão sendo fornecidos pela fabricante ZNSHINE SOLAR. Os módulos foram selecionados por sua durabilidade e desempenho e são projetados para resistir às condições tropicais da Indonésia, ao mesmo tempo que sustentam a confiabilidade de longo prazo do sistema. A entrada em operação está prevista para março de 2027. Uma vez em operação, espera-se que a instalação proporcione benefícios de descarbonização para as operações locais do setor de níquel. O projeto é apresentado como evidência de que a colaboração entre o desenvolvedor, a contratante de EPC e os credores internacionais pode apoiar tanto a gestão ambiental quanto a competitividade industrial. Seu desenvolvimento é descrito como um marco no caminho da Indonésia rumo a maior sustentabilidade e autossuficiência energética, à medida que o país continua a expandir a infraestrutura de energia renovável para a descarbonização industrial. artigo.texto: Senate blocks bill aimed at keeping data center costs off electric bills A Senate bill aimed at addressing higher electric costs tied to expanding data centers failed to advance, with Democrats arguing it did not go far enough. The Senate failed to advance a bill on Wednesday aimed at addressing higher electric bills as data centers expand across the country, falling three votes short despite bipartisan agreement on its goal. The vote was 57-43, short of the 60 votes needed to move forward. The measure had previously passed the House 417-3. Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, said, "This bill is the only path that we can take today that will lower electricity prices." Senate Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act, arguing it did not adequately address the issue. Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., said, "Let me be clear, this is nothing more than a messaging bill on the eve of an election." The bill would have required state utility regulators to consider making large power users, such as data centers, pay for the grid upgrades needed to serve them. However, it would not have mandated states to adopt that standard. Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said, "Senate Democrats want to make it mandatory for data centers to cover their own costs by law." Democrats have backed competing proposals that would go further. Heinrich's GRID Savings Act would direct federal regulators to require large electricity customers such as data centers to pay for infrastructure needed to connect them to the grid. Rep. Mike Johnson, R-La., said the Ratepayer Protection Act was "a codification of President Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge." The debate over data centers is growing beyond Washington, as communities across the country weigh the promise of new investment against concerns over electric bills and environmental impact. A recent AP-NORC/University of Chicago poll found about 6 in 10 Americans support limiting the number of new data centers, while 63% are concerned about their impact on electricity prices. Taylor Enterline, a Pennsylvania resident, said during a recent community meeting, "We really need strict regulations in place to protect ourselves from data centers." Trump has previously said communities that reject data centers risk "being backwards and poor." When asked about local concerns, Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said, "Nobody has to allow a data center in their hometown if they don't want. I mean, the people of the town will decide. But you know, I think that the places that have allowed data centers in voluntarily have seen the data centers produce more power than they consume, electricity prices have gone down." New economic data released Wednesday shows investment in AI infrastructure, such as data centers, is helping power economic growth. With the bill's failure, Congress has not imposed any new federal protections on data-center-related grid costs. Much of the responsibility remains with states, utility regulators and the agreements that communities strike with companies. The White House has its Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which participating tech companies have voluntarily agreed to cover new power and grid costs their data centers create rather than passing those costs on to existing customers. Husted's legislation was designed to codify key elements of that pledge. Tech companies have been making significant deals with local communities to build data centers. Meta says teachers in Louisiana's Richland Parish received annual bonuses of up to $50,000 because of increased tax revenue associated with its data center project. And on Tuesday, Amazon Web Services agreed to contribute $10 million toward a new career and technical education school in King George County, Virginia, as part of a planned $6 billion data center investment. Trump said Tuesday that people living near data centers could eventually see what he called a "dividend." The question remains whether those benefits outweigh concerns over power costs, water use and the impact on local communities.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition. FAW Group, GAIG Automobile Form Alliance FAW Group and Guangzhou Automobile Industry Group ("GAIG Automobile"), the controlling shareholder of GAC Group, signed a strategic cooperation framework agreement on September 29. The two state-owned automakers plan to strengthen coordination in assets and capital, technological innovation, and cross-regional industrial resources, drawing on their respective strengths in manufacturing, brands, global operations, and key automotive technologies. The agreement comes as GAC Group advances a major asset restructuring. Under a proposal disclosed on September 28, the listed automaker plans to acquire a 50% stake in FAW Toyota through a share issuance. The strategic partnership and the proposed transaction will move forward in parallel. China Unveils 2026-2030 Battery Plan China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and six other government departments have jointly released a plan for the new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), setting out development goals and key priorities. A key target is to achieve initial large-scale commercialization of all-solid-state batteries by 2030. The plan also calls for major advances in next-generation battery technologies, while targeting a cycle life of 15,000 cycles for long-life lithium batteries and product defect rates at the parts-per-billion level for leading manufacturers. The plan outlines 19 key tasks across five areas, including breakthroughs in all-solid-state battery industrialization, development of next-generation battery chemistries and a supply system centered on lithium-ion batteries alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries. It also calls for stronger battery recycling and the development of standards for emerging technologies. Beyond technology, China plans to promote the digital and green transformation of battery manufacturing and support battery companies expanding overseas. The policy also calls for international cooperation and measures to address overseas technical trade barriers, signaling an effort to strengthen China's battery industry across both technology development and global markets. XPeng's Carbon Credit Revenue Tops RMB 1 Billion XPeng has reportedly reached carbon credit deals with Porsche and several other international automakers covering emissions regulations in the EU, UK and Australia, generating more than RMB 1 billion ($140 million) in total revenue. XPeng's vice president confirmed that the reports were accurate, with the company expected to generate more than RMB 500 million in carbon credit revenue in 2026. The deals come as automakers face increasingly stringent emissions requirements in overseas markets. According to European Commission documents, Porsche has opted out of Volkswagen Group's internal CO₂ emissions pool and plans to form an independent open compliance pool for 2026–2027, with XPeng identified as a key partner. Under EU rules, automakers can form emissions pools and use surplus credits from low-emission manufacturers to offset excess emissions. XPeng's growing overseas sales are helping build its position as a potential carbon credit supplier. Its overseas deliveries topped 20,000 units in the second quarter, up 81% year on year, while overseas business accounted for more than 25% of revenue in the first half. From January to July, XPeng ranked first among Chinese new-energy brands in pure-electric sales in several European markets, including Norway, Denmark, France and Portugal. The development highlights a potential new revenue stream for Chinese automakers expanding overseas. As emissions regulations tighten globally, carbon credits are becoming an increasingly strategic asset, allowing automakers with strong EV sales to monetize their regulatory compliance advantages beyond vehicle sales themselves.

artigo.texto: Kandi Technologies’ China Battery Exchange Secures Follow-On Order for CATL Heavy-Truck Battery Swap Stations Second Batch Order in Two Months Underscores Growing Value of CATL Partnership Jinhua, China, Sept. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kandi Technologies Group, Inc. ("Kandi" or the "Company") (NASDAQ GS: KNDI), a global innovator in intelligent equipment and a technology-driven platform company, today announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, China Battery Exchange (Zhejiang) Technology Co., Ltd. ("China Battery Exchange"), has secured a second batch procurement order for heavy-truck battery swap station equipment from QIJI Energy, a subsidiary of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited ("CATL"). The order follows just two months after the initial batch order placed in July 2026, highlighting the continued commercial development of the Company's relationship with CATL. China Battery Exchange's cooperation with CATL began in August 2025, when the two companies signed a Framework Procurement Contract under which China Battery Exchange became part of CATL's global supplier network and began coordinating CATL's first order for a heavy-truck battery swap station, which was secured later that month. In January 2026, China Battery Exchange entered into a three-year strategic cooperation agreement to serve as a designated equipment supplier for QIJI Energy's heavy-truck battery-swapping program. In July 2026, QIJI Energy placed its first batch procurement order under the strategic cooperation agreement, marking China Battery Exchange's transition from product validation to commercial deployment. With its supplier relationship with CATL and approved-supplier status with QIJI Energy, China Battery Exchange is positioned to pursue additional equipment orders in connection with CATL's heavy-truck battery-swapping program . China Battery Exchange's Lin'an intelligent manufacturing facility commenced production in July 2026. With an expected annual production capacity of up to 200 battery swap stations, the facility is intended to support China Battery Exchange's ability to fulfill existing and potential future orders from CATL and serve additional battery swap equipment customers. Feng Chen, CEO of Kandi, commented, "We have received two batch orders within eight months of signing the QIJI Energy agreement, reflecting CATL's continued confidence in our products and delivery capabilities as well as the commercial potential of this partnership. We will continue to advance product development, expand production capacity and improve delivery efficiency to capture opportunities in the emerging heavy-truck battery swap market and establish battery swap equipment as a new growth engine for Kandi."

artigo.texto: Projetos de baterias colocalizados com usinas solares podem chegar ao primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência (LRCap) exclusivo para armazenamento com uma vantagem competitiva de até 35% em relação a projetos independentes. O cálculo é da Aurora Energy Research, que entende que a combinação permite compartilhar infraestrutura, utilizar a capacidade de conexão da usina solar e reduzir os impactos do curtailment, diminuindo o custo do projeto e abrindo espaço para ofertas mais competitivas no certame. Durante participação em painel do Storage Leaders, evento promovido pela Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar), Rodrigo Longo, research associate da consultoria, afirmou que a colocalização pode ser uma das principais estratégias para que os investidores tenham sucesso. Os dois leilões, marcados para os dias 2 e 4 de dezembro, receberam um número recorde de projetos cadastrados, segundo a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE). Ao todo, foram cadastrados 6.091, que somam 296,8 GW de potência. A expectativa da Aurora é de uma contratação de aproximadamente 2 GW. Com a disputa acirrada, ele considera que “todo upside precificado pode significar um salto” no certame e tornar o projeto mais competitivo. Nesse contexto, a colocalização pode representar uma vantagem relevante para os empreendimentos, ao permitir a redução dos custos de implantação e a utilização compartilhada de estruturas já existentes. Estratégias de competição Segundo o executivo, algumas estratégias de redução de custos estarão disponíveis para todos os participantes do certame, como a redução do custo de capital (Capex), principalmente do valor das baterias, e a otimização do dimensionamento dos projetos. Também será possível considerar receitas de arbitragem após o término do contrato de 15 anos do LRCap como parte da estratégia para reduzir o valor ofertado no leilão. Já os projetos colocalizados terão vantagens adicionais. Uma delas é o compartilhamento de infraestrutura. De acordo com Longo, a existência de uma subestação, estrutura de conexão e infraestrutura física associadas à usina solar pode permitir uma redução de 10% a 15% no Capex do projeto de bateria. Outra vantagem está relacionada ao uso do Montante de Uso do Sistema de Transmissão (Must), com potencial de redução adicional de até 20%. Como a geração solar e a bateria não precisam injetar energia simultaneamente, a capacidade de conexão utilizada pela usina solar pode ser aproveitada pela bateria em outros períodos. A terceira vantagem apontada por Longo é a mitigação do curtailment, jargão do setor elétrico para os cortes na geração renovável. Com a bateria, parte da energia que seria cortada pode ser armazenada e posteriormente injetada no sistema, reduzindo a exposição do ativo solar a esse risco. “A medida que os lances convergem, diferenciais competitivos vão definir o resultado do leilão. Quando a gente olha um bid comum versus um bid com colocation, a gente vê uma redução de 30% a 35%, que é uma margem competitiva muito grande dos projetos versus os outros”, afirmou. Baterias ainda dependem do mercado de capacidade Segundo Longo, a dinâmica do mercado de energia do Brasil ainda não oferece condições suficientes para viabilizar economicamente os projetos com uma estratégia baseada em arbitragem de preços. Internacionalmente, segundo ele, os sistemas de armazenamento costumam combinar três fontes principais de receita: mercado de capacidade, arbitragem no mercado de energia e serviços ancilares. No Brasil, como os preços não variam o suficiente para garantir os ganhos com arbitragem, os leilões de capacidade podem ser uma das principais formas de expansão do armazenamento no país. “Por ter PLD, por ter hidrelétrica sendo otimizada, a gente tem uma curva do pato que é suficiente para colocar as solares em estresse, mas não é o suficiente para fazer com que as baterias sejam economicamente viáveis só pelo mercado de energia” destacou, completando que, ao mesmo tempo, o cenário é de pressão nas renováveis, especialmente na fonte solar, com preços mais baixos, curtailment elevado, e exposição a modulação horária. Ele ainda pontuou que, mesmo com carregamento “gratuito” a partir do curtailment (usando a energia que seria jogada fora), os spreads intradiários limitados mantêm as receitas de arbitragem insuficientes para viabilizar as baterias ou reduzir os custos da solar. A consultoria estima que o spread médio de quatro horas precisa ser de, no mínimo, R$ 650/MWh durante 20 anos para fazer com que a bateria seja economicamente viável. Para um spread médio de quatro horas de R$ 250/MWh, seria necessária uma redução de 85% do capex da bateria para torna-lá economicamente viável nesta modalidade. A variação de preços da solar no Brasil é, em média, ainda menor. Dados apresentados pelo especialista apontam um spread intradiário de quatro horas para a energia solar no Brasil de R$ 166/MWh, patamar inferior ao de países como Chile ( R$ 344/MWh), Alemanha ( R$ 589/MWh) e Espanha (R$ 599/MWh). A Aurora Energy projeta uma necessidade de 8 GW de capacidade firme adicional até 2030. No cenário principal, essa necessidade seria dividida de forma equilibrada entre baterias e termelétricas. Já no cenário com maior participação de BESS, toda a capacidade adicional seria atendida por sistemas de armazenamento. Segundo a consultoria, nesse segundo cenário, a entrada de baterias poderia resultar, até 2035, em uma redução de quase 20% no curtailment e de aproximadamente 40% na volatilidade intradiária, o que reduziria significativamente o risco de modulação enfrentado pelos projetos solares. artigo.texto: Marisa Wanzeller, da Agência iNFRA A Echoenergia, braço de geração renovável do grupo Equatorial, defende que o leilão de baterias, agendado para dezembro deste ano, seja adiado caso a regra de custeio não mude. Atualmente, a legislação atribui aos geradores o pagamento dos encargos de contratação dos sistemas de armazenamento de energia. “A gente entende que um adiamento de dois a quatro meses, se necessário, é pouco relevante para efeitos do sistema elétrico e é um tempo suficiente para que a gente discuta e resolva o problema”, apontou o CEO da companhia, Liu Aquino, em entrevista à Agência iNFRA. Ele minimizou o risco de uma possível mudança de rota na política energética em 2027: “ninguém vai ser contra uma solução de menor custo marginal para o consumidor”. O executivo afirmou que o modelo vigente gera insegurança jurídica e levará a um leilão pouco competitivo, com custos altos de contratação devido aos riscos. Isso, na sua avaliação, prejudicaria a expansão das baterias no país. Medida Provisória Mesmo que o tema ainda passe por regulamentação na ANEEL (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica), a agência não poderá ultrapassar o dispositivo legal nos seus normativos. Dessa forma, torna-se necessária uma alteração da lei, aponta o CEO da Echoenergia. Para evitar que o certame seja postergado, ele sugere que o governo edite uma MP (Medida Provisória), diante da improbabilidade de o Congresso votar um projeto de lei antes de dezembro. Para ele, apesar da incerteza sobre a aprovação da medida e de sua transformação em lei posteriormente, realizar o leilão durante a vigência da MP daria mais segurança para o investidor do que o cenário atual. “O ideal era que houvesse um projeto de lei aprovado no Congresso. Agora, entre o cenário atual, que não tem nada, e o cenário de ter uma MP que vai ser discutida junto ao legislativo, a gente entende que o cenário da MP é de menor risco.” O deputado federal Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP) apresentou, ainda em julho, o PL (Projeto de Lei) 3.716/2026, que revoga o trecho da Lei 15.269/2025 que é considerado ruim pelos geradores. A matéria, contudo, ainda está parada e – em meio às eleições – tem poucas chances de tramitar nas duas casas legislativas a tempo da realização do certame. Custos O CEO da Echoenergia entende que os geradores vão subsidiar o leilão de baterias, uma vez que o benefício financeiro a eles será menor que o custo dos sistemas de armazenamento. Segundo levantamento da empresa, caso a alternativa de rateio entre todos os geradores conforme a flexibilidade da fonte prevaleça, o custo da contratação para os agentes eólicos e solares ficará em cerca de R$ 10,8 por MWh (megawatt-hora) a cada 5 GW (gigawatts) de potência. Considerando que toda a potência contratada seja utilizada para evitar curtailment, o benefício seria de R$ 2,6/MWh e R$ 4,7/MWh para os geradores eólicos e solares, respectivamente. “O leilão de bateria não está com propósito ou com racional econômico de atender os geradores e eles estariam pagando por isso. Na prática, o leilão de bateria estaria sendo subsidiado por investimentos que já foram feitos, por contratos e outorgas que estão no sistema há alguns anos e estariam pagando esta compra”, avalia Liu Aquino. Dessa forma, o executivo entende que a contratação deve ser bancada pelo consumidor, uma vez que o principal objetivo do leilão seria atender à demanda nos horários de “ponta”, quando a carga aumenta e a geração renovável cai. Na visão do CEO, a contratação dos sistemas de armazenamento irá reduzir a necessidade de contratação de térmicas, levando a um benefício econômico. Enquanto as baterias custariam entre R$ 600/MWh e R$ 800/MWh, as termelétricas seriam cerca de R$ 2.300/MWh. Acesso à transmissão Outro ponto que preocupa os agentes, segundo Liu Aquino, é a falta de regulamentação da Pnast (Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão) antes da realização do leilão de baterias. Isso porque, sem uma especificação, os sistemas de armazenamento terão que concorrer por espaço na rede durante as temporadas de acesso. O ideal, do ponto de vista da Echoenergia, seria o espaço na rede garantido para os lotes que ganharem o certame. “Esse processo de aprovação de conexão do sistema de bateria precisa ser sujeito somente a questões técnicas, e não a fluxo de potência. A restrição do fluxo de potência já tem que ser definida no leilão, porque não dá para o empreendedor entrar lá no leilão e assumir todos os compromissos para ver se vai poder conectar depois”, apontou.

artigo.texto: Candidates in 5th Congressional District race discuss AI and data centers at forum Republican and Democratic candidates weigh in on energy production and environmental concerns MONROE, La. (KNOE) - A forum was held Tuesday night for the 5th Congressional District race, featuring candidates from both major parties. Republican candidates Stewart Cathey, Misti Cordell, Michael Echols, Gabe Firment and Austin Magee attended the forum. On the Democratic side, Dan McKay and Pat Moore also weighed in. One topic at the forefront of the forum was artificial intelligence and data centers. When asked about energy production and environmental concerns surrounding the growing industry, Republican candidates Magee, Firment and Cathey said there needs to be some oversight. “What frustrates me is seeing that all of this red tape being cut for AI companies when the people need more power, we need better infrastructure, we can’t seem to get it. But the second that a small group of elites want to build God in a box and build these massive AI data centers, all red tape is immediately cut for them and they can have whatever they want,” Magee said. “The first thing that Congress needs to do is pass Ratepayer Protection Act which will ensure that as we see this growth of energy resources being spent here in this country that the companies that are actually using the energy are the ones that are paying it, not passing it on to the rate payer,” Cathey said. “You have to protect the consumer. It’s also absolutely imperative that we take care of our water and our natural resources. I passed House Resolution 374 last session to instruct the state to do just that, to study the use of one of our most precious natural resources, our water,” Firment said. Two Republicans, Cordell and Echols, said they see the lack of infrastructure for data centers as an opportunity to grow. “Nuclear is something that’s very effective and it’s also clean. Also hardening our grids. That’s something we have not done since the 70s. And the pellet technology. Part of this district is loggers, so any of the pellet technology could be a new version of energy,” Cordell said. “I passed a resolution that would encourage more nuclear, small nuclear reactor, and other types of fuels. I think Louisiana is a fuel-rich state. We just have to use the resources we’ve got to produce that,” Echols said. The Democratic candidates agreed with Magee, Cathey and Firment, saying there needs to be more regulations and laws placed on this type of growth. “I just believe that they have a lot of constitutional power. We’re going to have to look to make sure that we exercise that. And anything that is not healthy, not for the best interests of the people, then they’re going to have to make that decision,” Moore said. “We need some rules. And I say we get together in Congress and we make some rules to control the haphazard growth of these types of things,” McKay said. Republican Oscar “Omar” Dantzler and Democrat Antonio Wilson were not in attendance. The deadline to register to vote in the November election is Oct. 5, by mail or in person. artigo.texto: Addressing more than 20 global corporate executives at the High-Level and CEO Forum on Low-Emission Rice and Sustainable Agriculture in New York, the minister emphasized that carbon pricing mechanisms would allow investors to unlock additional financial value from verifiable emissions reductions in Indonesia. "Indonesia is facing a waste emergency that must be addressed immediately, one of which is through waste-to-energy. Therefore, the government is encouraging green investment in the waste sector as a priority," Zulkifli said in a statement on Tuesday (September 29). Zulkifli outlined three primary sectors open to green investment: sustainable agriculture through low-emission rice cultivation, waste-to-energy processing, and marine conservation through blue carbon development. As chair of the Carbon Economic Value (NEK) Steering Committee, he said Jakarta is streamlining regulatory frameworks and strengthening carbon trading governance to ensure high-credibility carbon assets. A key step came on July 6, 2026, when the Financial Services Authority (OJK) enacted POJK No. 10/2026, mandating that all exchange-traded carbon units be formally registered under the Carbon Unit Registry System (SRUK). OJK data as of August 31, 2026, revealed that 159 service users have registered on the Indonesian Carbon Exchange since its inception on September 26, 2023. Total transaction volume reached 1.98 million tons of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e), with a cumulative value of Rp93.90 billion (approximately US$5.24 million). Government projections indicate that the carbon pricing framework could mobilize up to US$5.80 billion in green investment while reducing greenhouse gas emissions by roughly 570 million tCO2e. Beyond waste management, Indonesia is seeking various international partners to scale up low-emission rice production to strengthen domestic food security while reducing agricultural methane emissions. Zulkifli noted that implementing low-emission rice cultivation on a large scale requires technological support, financing, market certainty, and clear economic benefits for farmers. He added that climate action must translate into concrete, field-level projects that directly benefit farmers and coastal communities. artigo.texto: Volkswagen slows gigafactory battery manufacturing plans in Ontario Subscribe to our free newsletter today to keep up to date with the latest manufacturing news. Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary PowerCo is pushing back the start of operations at its St. Thomas, Ontario, gigafactory to 2029, extending a timetable that had originally targeted the first battery cells for 2027 and giving the company more time to align production with changing market conditions. The shift adds two years to the schedule for one of Canada’s largest electric vehicle manufacturing investments, but it does not represent a retreat from the project because construction is continuing and the planned industrial scale remains largely unchanged. Volkswagen has said the plant could represent an investment of as much as C$7 billion, or about US$4.9 billion, by 2030, with annual production capacity eventually reaching up to 90 GWh and as many as 3000 direct skilled jobs supported at full development, alongside additional employment across the regional supply chain. The revised timetable matters beyond St. Thomas because battery manufacturers are trying to build factories that will operate for decades while the market they are designed to serve is evolving far more quickly, particularly as EV demand, vehicle platforms, battery chemistry and manufacturing economics continue to change. The two-year extension could strengthen the factory’s production ramp St. Thomas holds an important position in PowerCo’s global manufacturing network because Volkswagen has described the Ontario facility as the company’s first overseas gigafactory and its largest planned battery cell factory. At full expansion, the plant’s potential annual capacity of 90 GWh would make it a significant supplier to Volkswagen Group electric vehicle production in North America, giving the company a large regional source of battery cells while reducing dependence on longer and more complex international supply chains. The plant is based on PowerCo’s standardized factory concept and Unified Cell strategy, which are designed to create greater manufacturing consistency across several locations while still allowing battery cells to be adapted to different vehicle requirements and market conditions. Moving the start of operations from 2027 to 2029 changes the economics of the production ramp because a battery factory does not create value simply by having its equipment installed and its production lines available. Its financial performance depends heavily on utilization rates, production yields, material costs, customer demand and the ability to operate complex equipment at a sufficiently high volume to spread fixed costs across a large number of cells. Bringing major production capacity online before vehicle manufacturers are ready to absorb it can create an expensive mismatch between supply and demand, leaving costly machinery operating below its intended utilization rate while manufacturers continue to carry significant fixed operating expenses. A more gradual commissioning schedule gives battery producers more room to align cell output with vehicle programs, supplier contracts and regional demand rather than bringing large volumes online before the market can consistently support them. This approach has become more relevant as automakers reassess the pace of their electric vehicle investments and reconsider how quickly new platforms, factories and battery programs should be introduced across North America. The shift does not suggest that electrification has stopped, but it does show that manufacturers are becoming more selective about when individual factories should reach full production and how quickly capital-intensive capacity should be brought into service. For suppliers, logistics operators and industrial service providers, a two-year change to battery production can affect warehouse planning, inbound material contracts, equipment commissioning, workforce requirements, transport volumes and the timing of supplier investments tied to the plant. PowerCo can use the extra time to transfer technology from Europe The revised schedule could have another important consequence because the St. Thomas factory that begins producing batteries in 2029 may benefit from substantially more manufacturing experience than the plant that was originally expected to begin operations two years earlier. PowerCo began cell production at its Salzgitter gigafactory in Germany in late 2025, and Volkswagen has positioned that facility as the lead plant for subsequent battery operations in Valencia, Spain, and St. Thomas. That structure gives the Canadian operation more time to absorb production knowledge developed elsewhere in the network before it moves into high-volume manufacturing, which could influence how equipment is configured, how quality is managed and how operating procedures are designed. Battery manufacturing is particularly sensitive to this type of learning because improvements in production yield, quality control, energy consumption, material handling and equipment reliability can materially change the cost of every cell leaving a factory. Experience accumulated during the ramp-up of earlier plants can therefore affect the performance of later facilities, particularly when production teams are able to identify recurring problems before new factories reach commercial scale. Battery chemistry is evolving at the same time, creating another reason why a later production date could materially affect how the St. Thomas operation is configured when it begins manufacturing cells. Volkswagen, PowerCo and Chinese battery producer Gotion expanded their partnership in September 2026 to cover industrial production of lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, cells and cathode active materials in Europe, with Valencia expected to become an important European production hub for LFP technology. According to reports, this trial production is aimed at debugging, optimizing, and validating production equipment and manufacturing processes, in preparation for subsequent full-scale mass production. It is reported that in August 2022, CATL announced the construction of its second battery plant in Europe in Debrecen, Hungary, where the first battery cell facility began construction in the summer of 2023 and completed the installation of advanced production technologies and equipment by the spring of 2026. In August 2026, after obtaining the facility use permit, the company successively completed the prerequisite conditions required by relevant permits and IPPC (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control) permit requirements, and officially commenced trial production of the first two production lines at the first battery cell production facility on September 22.

artigo.texto: Alberto Kuba, CEO da WEG: 'não imaginávamos que teria esse boom' (Leandro Fonseca/Exame) Repórter Publicado em 30 de setembro de 2026 às 05h00. A multinacional fabricante de equipamentos elétricos WEG anunciou, entre sexta-feira, 25, e segunda-feira, 28, novos investimentos em baterias e geradores para atender à expansão de data centers e redes elétricas. BTG Pactual, Ativa Investimentos e Citi veem potencial de crescimento nos projetos, embora o impacto sobre os resultados deva ocorrer de forma gradual. A WEG (WEGE3) não esperava o ritmo que os data centers imprimiriam ao negócio de geradores. "Não imaginávamos que teria esse boom", afirmou Alberto Kuba, CEO da companhia, em entrevista para a edição 2026 do prêmio Maiores e Melhores, da Revista EXAME. Segundo o executivo, a demanda pelo equipamento ganhou força com a expansão dos data centers, que precisam de grupos geradores para garantir o fornecimento de energia em caso de interrupções. E a reação da companhia a esse movimento vem aparecendo cada vez mais nos investimentos.Na última sexta-feira, 25, a multinacional que fabrica equipamentos elétricos anunciou a ampliação da fábrica de baterias em Santa Catarina e, três dias depois, na segunda, 28, divulgou um investimento de US$ 165 milhões, cerca de R$ 869 milhões, para aumentar a produção de geradores na América do Norte. Os dois movimentos colocam a WEG em uma frente que combina geração, armazenamento e infraestrutura elétrica — e que ganhou força com o avanço dos data centers e a necessidade de redes mais robustas. Para o BTG Pactual (do mesmo grupo controlador da EXAME), Ativa Investimentos e Citi, os movimentos colocam a WEG em segmentos que podem sustentar o crescimento da companhia nos próximos anos, embora os efeitos dos novos investimentos sobre os resultados devam aparecer de forma gradual. No caso da iniciativa para ampliar a capacidade de produção de geradores na América do Norte, o projeto será dividido em duas fases e foi anunciado com foco na crescente demanda por soluções de geração de energia para aplicações críticas nos Estados Unidos, especialmente para atender à expansão dos data centers. A primeira fase receberá US$ 24 milhões para a aquisição e adequação de um prédio industrial próximo ao atual Parque Industrial Quma I, em Atotonilco de Tula, no México. A unidade será destinada à montagem de geradores e tem início de operação previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. Na segunda etapa, a WEG pretende investir US$ 141 milhões na construção de duas novas instalações industriais, em local ainda a ser definido na América do Norte. A estrutura terá produção verticalizada, incluindo a fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças. Com a conclusão da segunda fase, prevista para 2030, a capacidade global da WEG para fabricar geradores deverá passar das atuais 10 unidades por dia para cerca de 50. A produção será distribuída entre as fábricas da companhia no México, EUA, Brasil e China. O movimento amplia uma operação que já vem se beneficiando da expansão dos data centers. "O negócio de alternadores, sob a marca Marathon, tem apresentado um forte desempenho, apoiado pela robusta demanda por energia de reserva por parte dos data centers", escreveu o BTG em relatório nesta terça-feira, 29. Para o banco, o novo investimento aumenta a capacidade da WEG de atender a uma demanda que tende a exigir cada vez mais equipamentos para garantir o fornecimento de energia. O BTG considera o anúncio positivo e afirma que a expansão cria uma plataforma para o crescimento do negócio de geração de energia da companhia na América do Norte no médio prazo. O banco, porém, ressalta que o investimento não deve trazer uma contribuição relevante para o lucro imediatamente. Mas ressalta que "embora os gastos de capital iniciais impliquem uma contribuição limitada para os lucros no curto prazo, a adição de capacidade deve proporcionar uma plataforma para um maior crescimento dos negócios de geração de energia da WEG na América do Norte no médio prazo", afirmou. "A WEG realizará seu Investor Day nesta semana, onde esperamos mais detalhes sobre sua estratégia para aproveitar as oportunidades de crescimento no mercado norte-americano", acrescentou o banco sobre o evento que ocorre nesta sexta-feira, 2. O investimento em geradores veio três dias depois de outro anúncio relacionado à infraestrutura de energia. Na sexta-feira, 25, a WEG ampliou o projeto de sua fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, os BESS, em Itajaí, no litoral norte catarinense. O investimento previsto para a unidade passou de R$ 280 milhões para R$ 330 milhões, enquanto a capacidade anual de produção foi dobrada, de 2 para 4 gigawatts-hora (GWh). O início das operações está previsto para o segundo semestre de 2027. A expansão ocorre às vésperas do primeiro leilão de armazenamento de energia do país, previsto para dezembro de 2026. A expectativa é de crescimento da demanda por baterias para integrar fontes renováveis, como solar e eólica, ao sistema elétrico. Na avaliação da Ativa Investimentos, há aí uma oportunidade para a WEG. "Como temos discutido, as iniciativas de BESS e o crescimento de data centers são os principais gatilhos para destravar valor para a companhia", disse o analista da casa, Lucas Dias. O Citi também coloca os dois anúncios dentro de uma mesma tese. Para o banco, geradores para data centers e sistemas de armazenamento aumentam a exposição da WEG a dois segmentos ligados à expansão da infraestrutura energética. No caso dos geradores, o Citi destaca que a capacidade global da companhia deverá passar de 10 para 50 unidades por dia após a conclusão do projeto em 2030. Já no BESS, chama atenção para a velocidade da expansão: em sete meses, a WEG dobrou a capacidade planejada da fábrica e aumentou o investimento em R$ 50 milhões. artigo.texto: Anju Singh served as the host for a community forum in Cumberland County about data centers on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. Haley O'Brien / WITF Curious and concerned residents heard from experts, officials and organizers about data center development — and efforts to challenge it — during a community forum in Cumberland County on Tuesday. Environmental lawyers discussed the developments’ potential effect on the region’s water and power grid while organizers of local grassroots groups shared tips for residents concerned about proposed projects. John Werner is a member of Stewards of Cumberland County, an advocacy group that formed in response to data center developments. “We were one of the first organizations that formed locally, and we formed because people were not getting off Facebook,” he said. Werner spoke about what he called “the importance of people power.” “There are residents who have mounted robust challenges in municipalities all over the place and beat these data centers,” Werner said. “And our strongest weapon in this fight is one another.” Michael Ewall, founder of the Energy Justice Network, shared how the developments are projected to strain the power grid. “By 2030, we need about 60% increase in electric generation to meet the demand… which is largely being driven by the data center boom,” he said. Residents concerned about potential data center developments in their neighborhoods also asked what they can do to challenge the projects. “I feel very tiny in a very big space,” said Harrisburg resident Amara Nazario, who is in the early stages of forming a community group to advocate against proposed developments in Swatara Twp., Dauphin County. “I’m still just wrapping my head around everything and jumping into a fight,” she said. Werner recommended those who live in a community with a project in the works to find a way to slow down the process. “The more hurdles that you can throw up, the more inconvenient it is for the developers,” he said. Amy Zeigler, from the group Protect South Hanover PA, had flyers and a presentation prepared to show the impact of a proposed data center on surrounding communities. She suggested groups work together and share each other’s strengths, including graphic design, public speaking and organizational skills. Dauphin County Commissioner Justin Douglas did not say he supports data centers. But he said municipalities are struggling to balance budgets and these expensive developments can provide significant revenue. artigo.texto: - Colombia’s Environment Ministry plans to revoke Decree 973 of 2026, which established rules for the country’s carbon market. - The government cited procedural issues and plans to develop a replacement framework with broader participation. - Environment Minister Fabio Arjona wants to strengthen the national emissions registry and attract private investment. Colombia’s government is moving to revoke regulations governing its carbon market, reopening a policy framework adopted only weeks ago under former President Gustavo Petro, local news website La Silla Vacía reported Tuesday, citing Environment Minister Fabio Arjona. Arjona announced the decision during Medellín Climate Week, saying the government would begin the process of withdrawing Decree 973 of 2026. The measure was issued shortly before Petro left office and introduced requirements for carbon projects, including emissions verification, community participation and government oversight of international credit sales. The Environment Ministry said its review found that the Finance Ministry had not participated in matters within its remit and that opinions from other government agencies were still pending when the decree was issued. The ministry also said the final text had undergone substantial changes without being republished for public comment. Government Plans Replacement Framework The government says revoking the decree is intended to correct those procedural issues while developing a new regulatory system involving communities, territories, private companies and public agencies. Arjona said the government aims to build a stronger National Registry of Greenhouse Gas Emission Reductions, known as Renare, and establish rules intended to encourage private capital to support conservation and emissions reductions. He said the administration expects to have a new version of Renare ready within three months. Relevant: Former Colombia President Iván Duque Takes Key Role In Global Carbon Accounting Push The decree had also extended potential project durations, allowing some emissions reduction projects to operate for up to 15 years and removal projects for as long as 40 years. Industry representatives nevertheless raised concerns that government approval between project phases could increase costs and deter foreign investment. The ministry said existing rules will remain in effect while the replacement framework is developed. Read more: Amazon Tribes Triumph In Landmark Carbon Credit Lawsuit In Colombia

artigo.texto: A expansão da inteligência artificial no mundo inteiro tem levado à corrida pela construção de data centers para suprir as necessidades de processamento desta tecnologia, e o Brasil é um palco importante para este desenvolvimento. Ao mesmo tempo que as empresas querem expandir os seus negócios, crescem as notícias sobre o impacto da construção de data centers nas cidades. Um exemplo é a cidade de Paracatu, em Minas Gerais, onde vereadores da Câmara Municipal descobriram que em breve a obra de um data center começará na região. O site O Eco fez uma reportagem sobre a referida obra, mostrando que não se trata de um data center qualquer: o equipamento terá a potência de 1 gigawatt, “maior que a soma total de todos os data centers atualmente instalados no país, que consomem cerca de 800 megawatts”. Só que a construção de data centers pode provocar danos ambientais, alto consumo de água e aumento do custo de energia para o consumidor, sem trazer benefícios reais para a população e para o país. Este assunto foi discutido em audiência pública no Senado em 4 de agosto na Comissão de Ciência e Tecnologia (CCT). O diretor-executivo do Instituto de Defesa do Consumidor (Idec), Igor Britto, ressalta que os data centers de inteligência artificial representam um alto consumo de energia elétrica sem capacidade de adaptação horária das atividades. “Temos empreendimentos de vários setores produtivos que já são organizados e se controlam para, por exemplo, evitar operar e consumir energia nos horários de maior pico. Isso não acontece com os data centers, que vão acabar sobrecarregando o sistema nesses horários. Todos nós pagamos. É necessário ter infraestrutura para mais geração, para mais distribuição, e o pior é que todos esses custos também são bancados pela tarifa. Cidades onde existem data centers tiveram aumento considerável na conta de energia e, quanto ao consumo de água, algumas residências chegam a ficar sem o abastecimento. As cooperativas nas diversas regiões do país precisam ficar atentas aos projetos vindouros, principalmente após a sanção da Lei 15.504, que cria incentivos fiscais para estimular a instalação de data centers, os centros de processamento de dados, e favorecer investimentos em inteligência artificial (IA) no Brasil. Apesar das preocupações com geração de energia e consumo de água, os data centers podem também ser uma forma de expansão tecnológica das cooperativas. Oportunidades No Paraná, um grupo de investidores apresentou em julho, ao Governo do Estado e a instituições paranaenses, a proposta de implantação de um super data center no município de Pinhais, na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba. Na oportunidade, os investidores informaram que têm interesse em realizar negócios com produtos do agronegócio das cooperativas paranaenses, contemplando especialmente soja, milho e proteínas animais. Segundo eles, o grupo projeta movimentar grandes volumes de exportação e conta com estrutura logística própria, incluindo frota e terminais portuários. Foi ainda mencionada a possibilidade de facilitar a aquisição de matérias-primas para a produção de fertilizantes e o fomento na região. Apesar de acreditarem ser um projeto promissor, seguir compromissos de sustentabilidade é necessário para o avanço do projeto.

artigo.texto: Community voices concerns ahead of new AI data center in Jefferson Davis County JEFFERSON DAVIS COUNTY, Miss. (WDAM) - A digital infrastructure campus is coming to Jefferson Davis County. The developer, Eagle Rock Partners, held a public hearing Tuesday evening to address concerns. Some residents worry about water usage, power rates and the amount of noise the campus will cause, while others want to have a say in whether they build it or not. “We’re concerned about how the traffic for them trying to build this is going to affect our daily lives,” Bassfield Resident Patti Warren said. “There’s a lot involved in all of this, and we just think that the community should have a right to be able to vote.” The campus will cover 800 acres of land near Gum Swamp Road and the Covington County line. Eagle Rock Members say it will offer a projected 200 full-time operational jobs and over 1,000 construction jobs. Economic Development Association Executive Director Gary Russell Bass understands the negative feelings surrounding AI data centers, but he wants the public to understand the opportunities this will bring to the county. “I’ve done a lot of research on this company, I’ve done a lot of research on what they’re saying, and I think that the information that they’re trying to provide the community is a step in the right direction,” Bass said. “I just hope that everybody would come with an open mind, and get all of their questions answered.” Ken Lober with Eagle Rock Partners wanted the meeting to leave no box unchecked. With a project like this already in motion, Lober wanted the community to be involved and know the “why” behind the project. “We aspire to be completely transparent, and this is a big step towards that,” Lober said. “To have the community come out, ask any questions they want, walk through the facts of what this project is, then work with the economic development agency, the county supervisors, and to be able to make sure that the county engineer and everybody validate what we’re saying we’re going to do, and that we do it.” This campus is an estimated $6 billion capital investment. artigo.texto: Porto Central pode receber investimento em data centers Porto estuda estrutura para receber data centers, com oferta de energia e conexão por cabos submarinos O Porto Central, em Presidente Kennedy, desenvolve um projeto para implantar um hub de data centers voltado a empresas do Brasil e do exterior. A iniciativa pretende aproveitar a oferta de energia do Espírito Santo e a infraestrutura do complexo portuário para criar uma nova frente de desenvolvimento econômico. Segundo Fabrício Cardoso Freitas, CEO da Macro Investimentos e membro do Conselho de Administração, o empreendimento poderá contar com energia, água, áreas disponíveis e a estrutura logística do porto, incluindo a possibilidade de conexão ferroviária. Freitas afirmou que o Porto Central já desenvolveu e licenciou 5 gigawatts (GW) de capacidade e destacou a segurança de fornecimento associada ao terminal de Gás Natural Liquefeito (GNL). Para ele, essas condições podem atender à crescente demanda mundial por infraestrutura de processamento de dados. Outro ponto em estudo é a chegada de cabos submarinos de telecomunicações. O porto já possui autorização para receber um cabo, e as tratativas avançam. A proposta é receber, processar e distribuir dados para o mercado brasileiro e também para o exterior. O projeto ainda está em fase de concepção e estruturação. A próxima etapa será definir o modelo do empreendimento, dimensionar infraestrutura e insumos, como energia e água, e prospectar empresas que possam utilizar os futuros data centers.
